title: Highlights from Pope Leo’s historic, 12-day tour of South America
summary: They turned out in their millions to greet Pope Leo as he made his way around Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on a gruelling 12-day tour of the South America.
story: LIMA, Peru — They turned out in their millions to greet Pope Leo as he made his way around Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on a grueling 12-day tour of the South American nations, weeks after undergoing successful surgery for lung cancer.
Pope keeps energetic pace in trip to South America after surgery

For some — particularly those in Argentina, which had not received a papal visit since Pope John Paul II in 1987 — it was the first time they would get to see a pontiff in person. A record 2.5 million people flooded onto the streets of Buenos Aires last week to try and catch a glimpse of Leo.

The Vatican dubbed it a “homecoming” tour for the 71-year-old, as the Chicago-born pontiff, who is also a citizen of Peru, spent the final six days in the country where he lived for decades and served as a bishop until 2023.
NBC News takes a look at some of the highlights from his trip.
Montevideo, Uruguay

After a 17-hour flight from Rome, Leo and his entourage touched down in Uruguay’s capital, Montevideo. Praising the Lord and thanking his wonderful medical assistants, Leo said that while some had questioned whether he would be able to make the trip because of his recent surgery, he “had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward.”

title: Lindsay Clancy retrial scheduled for March over the strangulation deaths of her three children
summary: Lindsay Clancy’s retrial for the killings of her three young children in 2023 has been set for March, a Massachusetts judge said Monday.
story: Lindsay Clancy’s retrial for the killings of her three young children in 2023 has been set for March, a Massachusetts judge said Monday.

Clancy and her team appeared in court for a status hearing that set the date for her retrial. Judge William Sullivan last week did not rule in favor of the defense’s motion to dismiss all charges against Clancy, paving the way for a retrial.
The retrial will start March 29, giving both sides four months to prepare. The final pretrial hearing will be March 18.

Clancy’s first trial ended in a mistrial in September after jurors said a holdout prevented the nine women and three men from reaching a unanimous decision. In the weeks following the mistrial, defense attorney Kevin Reddington filed a motion to dismiss the three murder charges.

Clancy is accused of strangling her three children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months old — with exercise bands on the night of Jan. 24, 2023, before throwing herself out of her bedroom window in a suicide attempt that left her paralyzed and in a wheelchair. She has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder.

Her defense has argued that she was in the throes of postpartum psychosis when she carried out the killings and therefore was unaware of her actions at the time. The prosecution, however, argued that she planned the killings ahead of time and was not actually in psychosis when she murdered the children.
It remains unclear whether the arguments on both sides will remain the same in the next trial.
Reddington, after court Monday, said he was surprised that the prosecution intends to pursue the first-degree murder charges against Clancy for a second time.
“I mean, they have an indictment, they have a right to go forward on it,” Reddington said. “I’m a little disappointed with the way it shook out today, but they have a right to do that.”

After Sullivan ruled against the motion to dismiss Clancy’s charges, the prosecution had to decide whether to move ahead with a new trial. Prosecutors could also have reduced the charges, moved to a bench trial, offered a plea deal, or dropped the charges altogether.

Martin Weinberg, an attorney on Clancy’s defense team, argued for the motion to dismiss charges, saying in court Nov. 2 that the prosecution had to meet the manifest necessity standard to warrant a mistrial and, in turn, a retrial. He argued that the court should have questioned the holdout juror when he refused to participate in negotiations, and if his reasons were personal, the court could have discharged him, allowing deliberations to continue with another juror. That did not happen, he said.

The jury foreperson returned three deadlock notes before Sullivan declared a mistrial, but Sullivan did not voir dire the juror — meaning question the juror to determine whether they could be fair and impartial — and declared a mistrial before replacing him with an alternate. Reddington then attempted a last-minute emergency stay, but Supreme Judicial Court Associate Justice Dalila Argaez Wendlandt later denied it.

On Nov. 2, the prosecution argued that the court must determine whether manifest necessity was met based on what happened in court and what the court knew at the time of the mistrial — not what happened afterward or what the media revealed. It also asked the judge to deny the motion Oct. 29.

Following the mistrial, several other jurors spoke out, including the jury foreperson, and described the holdout as someone who refused to participate in discussions. They also said he did not apply the reasonable doubt standard when wanting to convict Clancy of first-degree murder.
The holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, has since said he has felt harassed since the end of the trial and insisted in an interview that he “didn’t have any doubts.”
On Nov. 9, Sullivan also ruled on two other motions discussed in court the week prior.

Sullivan denied Clancy’s motion to question the holdout juror in the trial and examine court records related to his service. The prosecution was also handed a loss on one of its motions in court last week — Sullivan rejected its bid to prevent lawyers from freely discussing the case with the media.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Clancy’s initial trial captivated the nation, prompting online sleuths to probe the unique case — and reach their own conclusions. For the duration of the trial, a faction of posters insisted that Clancy couldn’t have carried out the killings, and that her then-husband, Patrick Clancy, did instead, framing her.
Reddington on Monday said he wouldn’t be surprised if the second trial gets the same national attention.

“I don’t know what the temperature would be as far as media, and I think it would probably be pretty intense,” he said, adding that Clancy’s case covers a lot of issues that “a lot of people are concerned with,” such as mental health and women’s health.
In an interview days after the mistrial, Reddington said Clancy rejects the conspiracy theories about Patrick Clancy. He also said Clancy, at the time, “was not very good” and remained “suicidal.”
On Monday, he reiterated that Clancy and her family are “not good” but that her family is “very supportive.”

If you or someone you know is in crisis, call 988 to reach the National Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 800-273-8255, text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.

title: Robert Pattinson named as the newest James Bond
summary: Actor Robert Pattinson has been tapped to take on the role of James Bond as Amazon MGM Studios seeks to continue the blockbuster film franchise.
story: Agent 007 has a new face.
Actor Robert Pattinson has been tapped to take on the role of James Bond as Amazon MGM Studios seeks to continue the blockbuster film franchise.

The studio announced the “Twilight” and “The Batman” alum as its choice to pick up the secret agent mantle, making the 40-year-old the latest in a list of leading men who have had the honor of playing the spy.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement, adding, “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”
The news comes after years of speculation over who would take over the role after Daniel Craig announced in 2019 that he was leaving the franchise.
In the last week, rumors over Craig’s successor centered on Pattinson after a report from Puck suggested he was the front-runner.

Denis Villeneuve is directing the new Bond film, which further fueled the speculation given that Pattinson collaborated with Villeneuve on the “Dune” franchise. The third installment of that franchise hits theaters in December.

From starring in A24’s indie film “The Drama” to blockbuster epic “The Odyssey,” Pattinson has had a massive year, joining the handful of Hollywood stars who have dominated the big screen. Most recently, he starred as “Dateline NBC” alum Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” the A24 film that follows the TV personality’s “To Catch a Predator” era.
The script for the new Bond film is being written by Steven Knight, who created the TV series “Peaky Blinders.”

Amazon MGM Studios, the tech giant’s film unit, took over “creative control” of the James Bond series under a new deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The deal was announced in February 2025.
Now, “Spider-Man” producer Amy Pascal and “Harry Potter”  producer David Heyman will take on the latest installment, producing through Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
In a statement, Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, emphasized that Pattinson’s casting is helping to “usher in a new era of Bond.”

“This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward,” he said, praising the “world-class creative team in place” that will be carrying on the franchise’s legacy.

Bond fans have had many thoughts as to who would take on the mantle, with many hoping that Idris Elba would be tapped as the next British super spy. But Elba told People magazine in August that he was never truly in the race to become the next Bond.
In recent months, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner reportedly also tested for the role.

Bond has evolved into one of the most coveted roles for male actors in the United Kingdom. The book-to-screen character written by Ian Fleming has had a unique staying power across generations, beginning with Sean Connery in the 1962 film “Dr. No.” The Scottish actor played Bond across seven films and two decades.

George Lazenby, the only Australian to play Bond, starred in 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.” He only played Bond for that film, which some have called one of the most underrated. Among the film’s fans is director Christopher Nolan, who called it his favorite of the franchise.

But it was Roger Moore who was considered to be the one who replaced Connery in the iconic spy franchise. Moore was often criticized in comparison to Connery, but he was chosen to star in seven of the franchise’s movies.

After Moore’s final Bond film in 1985, actor Timothy Dalton was given a smaller stint as the British agent. Dalton starred in two films, including “Licence to Kill,” in which he chose to portray Bond with a darker, more serious tone than previously seen by fans.

The character took another turn when Pierce Brosnan was given the role. Brosnan said he grew up adoring both Connery and Moore in the role, telling GQ in 2014 that it never felt “real” to him that he held the job.
Brosnan was told following his final Bond film, “Die Another Day,” that the character was being rethought and negotiations with his agent to continue his role had stopped.

“And that certainly dug into the solar plexus of life, just because it was pretty gut-wrenching and because it had been somewhat heralded that I was coming back,” the Irishman told GQ. “So, it’s just business. And you’re the one caught in the crosshairs.”
Brosnan was replaced by Craig, who was lauded by critics and fans alike after he made his 007 debut in the franchise’s “Casino Royale” installment.

The actor chose to leave the fictional spy life behind after five films, saying on “The Graham Norton Show” in 2021 that he was glad to be leaving on his own terms even though it was an emotional decision.
“I’m grateful to the producers for allowing me to do that,” Craig said. “But I shall miss it. I’ll probably be incredibly bitter when the new person takes over.”
In a statement posted to X, Ian Fleming Publications, which owns and manages the literary rights to James Bond, praised the casting news.

“As Bond himself reflects at the end of Moonraker when facing the fact that the object of his affections is engaged to another man, ‘He must play the role which she expected of him. The tough man of the world. The Secret Agent. The man who was only a silhouette.’ We look forward to Pattinson stepping into that silhouette and making it his own,” the account wrote. “We have no doubt that Ian Fleming would be amazed at the longevity of his creation and the fact that the world is still hungry for tales of the world’s greatest spy.​”
Online, many diehard Pattinson fans — particularly millennials who identified as “Twihards” — were thrilled by the star’s newest role.
“A great day for us Team Edward girlies,” wrote one X user, referring to Pattinson’s role as brooding, telepathic vampire Edward Cullen.

Several users even posted a scene from the first “Twilight” film, released in 2008, in which Pattinson’s Edward is seen opening the car door for his romantic interest Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) after one of their peers announces the school dance theme is Monte Carlo.
“Gambling, tuxedos and Bond, James Bond,” one of the characters says, before it cuts to Pattinson and Stewart.
“Twilight literally predicted Robert Pattinson being James Bond btw,” wrote one X user who shared the clip.
Within minutes after the news dropped, many had also already cut thirsty fan edits compiling clips of the actor in his various roles and appearances.
But there were many who blasted the choice. “robert pattinson as bond is such a boring choice man, please for the love of god choose an unknown,” one X user noted.
And others who worried that Pattinson will be too busy with Bond for other roles.
“we’re never getting that second Batman movie…” wrote one X user.
“He’ll do great, I’m sure of it,” wrote another user. “But man am I still disappointed.”

title: Supreme Court rejects challenge to Maryland’s ‘sensitive places’ gun ban
summary: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear a broad challenge to Maryland’s restrictions on people carrying firearms in a broad range of public areas.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear a broad challenge to Maryland’s restrictions on people carrying firearms in a broad range of public areas.

The court for now sidestepped a chance to define what exactly is a “sensitive place,” a term used in previous rulings to describe locations where guns could be banned. As a result, the Maryland restrictions remain in place.
The various state measures restrict carrying firearms in state parks, on public transport, on school property, in healthcare facilities and in places that sell alcohol.

The court’s 6-3 conservative majority has frequently backed gun rights in a series of rulings that have expanded the scope of the Constitution’s Second Amendment, which protects the right to bear arms.

Justice Clarence Thomas, part of that majority, wrote a brief statement agreeing with the court’s decision not to hear the Maryland case in part because so many distinct provisions were being challenged, saying “the breadth of petitioners’ challenge would complicate our review.”
But he signaled interest in a future case that would be “more narrowly focused.”
Thomas added he is “skeptical” that the various Maryland provisions are in fact lawful.
For Subscribers

The various Maryland provisions being challenged include some enacted in 2023 in the aftermath of the Supreme Court’s ruling a year earlier that expanded gun rights by finding for the first time there is a right to carry a firearm outside the home.
That 2022 ruling set a new test for assessing gun restrictions, putting the legal spotlight on both new and long-standing laws.
When considering gun laws, judges must now focus solely on whether a law comports with a historical understanding of the Second Amendment.

But in a 2008 ruling when the court first recognized an individual right to bear arms, Justice Antonin Scalia wrote in the majority opinion that “nothing in our opinion should be taken to cast doubt on ... laws forbidding the carrying of firearms in sensitive places such as schools and government buildings.”
For Subscribers
Gun rights advocates concede that there is a long history of banning firearms in certain locations, including polling places, courthouses and legislatures.
But they argue that states like Maryland have gone too far in extending those bans to modern-day public places such as airports and entertainment districts.

Maryland officials are “openly hostile” to gun rights, with the restrictions so broad they severely limit the ability to carry firearms in public at all, lawyers challenging the Maryland law said in court papers. They represent individual Maryland residents who want to carry guns in public as well as four gun rights groups.
Other states with similarly broad restrictions include California, New York, New Jersey and Hawaii.

Maryland Attorney General Anthony Brown, a Democrat, urged the court not to take up the case, saying in court papers that there are “vast areas of shared consensus” over which locations should be considered sensitive places.
Since the 2022 Supreme Court ruling, lower courts have wrestled with how to apply the new test to modern contexts.

The Supreme Court itself appeared to acknowledge that in a 2024 ruling when it upheld a federal law that prohibits people subject to domestic violence restraining orders from possessing a firearm, a decision that angered gun rights activists.

In its most recent gun rights ruling, the court in June struck down a Hawaii law that sought to limit people bringing firearms onto private properties open to the public. The Maryland law contained a similar provision that was struck down by a lower court and is not at issue in the latest appeal.

title: Supreme Court rejects Trump over academic funding cuts related to DEI
summary: The Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump’s move to abruptly cancel academic funding for researchers in California over his opposition to DEI initiatives.
story: WASHINGTON —  The Supreme Court on Monday rejected President Donald Trump’s move to abruptly cancel academic funding for researchers in California because his administration deemed the projects to be inconsistent with policies such as his opposition to DEI initiatives.

The court left in place lower court rulings that said the government violated the free speech rights under the Constitution’s 1st Amendment by terminating grants issued to University of California researchers.

Upon taking office in January 2025, Trump issued several executive orders telling agencies to ensure funding was consistent with his views opposing diversity, equity and inclusion programs, as well as such issues as climate change and transgender rights.
For Subscribers
At issue in the Supreme Court appeal were grants issued by the National Science Foundation and the National Endowment for the Humanities.
In total, the federal government tried to end $324 million in funding to University of California institutions as part of a nationwide purge, although some funding has since resumed.
For Subscribers

Affected researchers sued, saying that the decisions discriminated against them based on their views. They alleged that the grants were cut based on keyword searches looking for words or phrases disfavored by the administration, such as “diversity” or “climate change.”
Both a federal judge and the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals agreed with the plaintiffs that the terminations violated free speech rights.

But in a separate part of the case not at issue in the Supreme Court, the appeals court ruled that the plaintiffs would have to file a separate lawsuit in the Court of Federal Claims if they wanted to recoup lost funding.

title: Trump says he ‘would not mind’ if Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO
summary: President Donald Trump said he “wouldn’t mind” Jensen Huang being reinstated as CEO of Nvidia after he resigned.
story: President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that he “would not mind” if Jensen Huang were reinstated as CEO of Nvidia after he resigned following allegations of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a woman believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset.

“I would not mind that,” the president said when asked about a reinstatement, adding that he thinks the ex-Nvidia chief, who resigned last week after the allegations were reported, had “learned a big lesson.”
After Huang stepped down, Trump said he would support former Apple CEO Tim Cook as Huang’s successor at Nvidia, which he noted again in comments to White House reporters Monday.

The president also told reporters that he did not know if Alice Huang, one of the women Jensen Huang allegedly conducted an affair with, was actually a spy, despite a U.S. intelligence assessment that she was working for Beijing.
“I don’t know that she is a spy,” Trump said as he prepared to leave for his Asia trip.

Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia sent ripples through the technology industry and raised questions about the sector’s vulnerabilities to Chinese espionage operations, which could have national security implications.

It’s also led to volatile trading Monday in major U.S. stock indexes, of which Nvidia, worth more than $3 trillion, has formed a major component. On Monday, Nvidia shares fell more than 4% in early afternoon trading. and are down by more than 10% over the past week.

Nvidia has hired an outside law firm to investigate the allegations against Jensen Huang, whose relationships may have violated company policies and who presided over export arrangements that raised concerns about Nvidia chips reaching China.

Asked by a reporter what he would say to Americans who are concerned that national security was put at risk because of his close relationship with Jensen Huang and the business leader’s alleged affair with a suspected spy, Trump said that national security “was not put at risk.”

Two senior U.S. officials previously told reporters they did not believe Trump would raise the Alice Huang espionage investigation with Chinese President Xi Jinping. One of the officials said Nvidia “should not really have any bearing on the trip.”
Asked Monday why he was not planning to confront Xi about the alleged spying on Nvidia, Trump replied, “I may.”

Trump’s openness to the possibility of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia comes as an online petition supporting the idea has garnered about 180,000 signatures. Some high-profile Silicon Valley personalities, including Elon Musk and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, said they backed the effort to restore Huang. It is not clear who is behind the petition; a message sent via a contact form to organizers was not returned.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Yet the White House itself appears to be divided. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a “dramatic shake-up” of Nvidia’s leadership in the wake of the Huang scandal, telling Fox News that Nvidia’s board should look outside the company for its next chief executive.
Bessent also suggested that other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over whether they complied with U.S. export control laws.
At the Commerce Department, which sets export controls, Bessent’s national security concerns appeared to be both elevated and undermined Monday by Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Elevated because the agency’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued a new chip-export rule that would close a loophole used to skirt the current export restrictions for advanced American AI semiconductors.

But the agency undermined it, as well, because in announcing the rule, the Commerce Department specifically attributed the new restrictions to the Treasury Department and the National Security Council, effectively distancing itself from its own rule.

title: Richard Sterban, distinctive bass vocalist of The Oak Ridge Boys, dies at 83
summary: Richard Sterban, a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley and the inimitable bass singer for The Oak Ridge Boys on their hit “Elvira,” died Saturday.
story: Richard Sterban, a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley and the inimitable bass singer for The Oak Ridge Boys, died Saturday from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia after a battle with cancer.
He was 83.

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers,” his family said in a statement. “Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus.”
Sterban joined The Oak Ridge Boys in 1972 after leaving his job as Elvis Presley’s backup vocalist, a press release states, citing Sterban’s desire to “be in the best vocal group in the world.”
Fellow member of The Oak Ridge Boys, William Lee Golden, said Sterban’s death was a “sad day.”
“GOD Bless and Comfort his Family through this Valley of Sorrow Rest in Peace my Friend,” he wrote on Facebook.

The group won five Grammy Awards and four Academy of Country Music Awards, including Top Vocal Group and Album of the Year, and the prestigious Cliffie Stone Pioneer Award in 2008. It was inducted into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame in 2000 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015.
The Academy of Country Music said Sterban “helped shape one of country music’s most recognizable sounds” and said it was saddened by his death.

“I grew up in radio hearing Richard’s voice come out of every speaker in America. That ‘oom-pa-pa-mow-mow’ on ‘Elvira’ was pure joy,” Academy of Country Music CEO Andy Schuon said in a statement. “He was a gentleman and a believer who carried gospel into country and pop, and brought millions of fans along with him.”

Sterban, born on April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, developed his love for music at a young age. He started singing at 6 years old as a soprano in a Sunday school and as a tenor in his seventh-grade glee club. By the time he started eighth grade, his voice had dropped to bass.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
After graduating from Collingswood High School, Sterban studied music at Trenton State College, now The College of New Jersey.
Sterban helped found the Keystones, a gospel quartet that tenor Joe Bonsall sang in. Bonsall was also a member of The Oak Ridge Boys. He died in 2024.

Sterban’s path led him to sing in the Stamps Quartet, which Presley had hired to sing behind him. He performed with Presley for about a year and a half, until The Oak Ridge Boys called, in need of a bass singer. Sterban joined the group, replacing Noel Fox.

Johnny Cash featured the group in his touring show and helped them sign to Columbia Records in 1973, but success did not come overnight, and their two albums drew little notice. While performing, the group caught the attention of music manager Jim Halsey, who convinced them to try country music. They later signed with Halsey, making hit after hit. “Y’all Come Back Saloon” reached No. 3 on the country chart in 1977 and “I’ll Be True to You” climbed to No. 1, the press release states.

In 1981, the group released “Elvira,” which also hit No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart, sold more than two million copies, was named Single of the Year by both the Country Music Association and the Academy of Country Music, and won a Grammy Award.
The group also performed for four presidents, from Gerald Ford to George W. Bush.
Sterban is survived by his wife, Donna, and his five children.

title: Grammys 2027 nominees: Raye, Rosalía and women artists dominate major categories
summary: RAYE, Rosalía and women artists dominate Grammy 2027 nominees list
story: Baby, where the hell is her Grammy?

Female artists led the 2027 Grammy nominee list, which was unveiled during an early morning livestream Monday. The nominees were announced by a star-studded lineup of past Grammy winners and nominees, including Alan Menken, David Guetta and Pharrell Williams.
Nominees across 100 categories were selected by 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy. Eligible artists released their music during the period encompassing Aug. 31, 2025 — Aug. 28, 2026.
The 69th Grammy Awards will take place at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Feb. 7. The show will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu.
Here are some of the key takeaways from this year’s announcement.
Raye and Rosalía lead nominees

British singer-songwriter Raye came out on top with a whopping 11 nominations, including for song, record and album of the year. The 28-year-old rose to the top of the charts this year with her hit, “Where Is My Husband!” She now joins Beyoncé in tying the record for the most nods earned by a female artist in a single  year.

Rosalía, who recently made history at the Latin Grammys by becoming the first female artist to win album of the year three times, snagged nine nominations. “LUX,” her fourth full-length album, features 13 different languages.

Olivia Rodrigo snagged seven nods for her latest album “you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love.” Phoebe Bridges, Ella Langley and collaborator Miranda Lambert all also earned seven nominations apiece.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Leaving space for ‘Wicked’
It may feel like an eternity ago that “Wicked: For Good” was released in theaters.

But Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande notched a best traditional pop vocal performance nomination for their song “For Good,” from the sequel to the 2024 Broadway adaptation about an unlikely friendship between two witches.
Erivo starred as the Wicked Witch of the West and Grande as the Good Witch, Glinda in the Universal Pictures film. (NBC News and Universal Pictures share Comcast as a parent company.)
Erivo and Grande are no strangers to the Grammys, having won two Grammys and three Grammys, respectively.
The film was also nominated in the best score soundtrack for visual media and best song written for visual media categories
Dolly Parton receives posthumous nods
The “Queen of Country” music, who died at age 80 in August, was among the nominees in the best country duo and group performance categories.
Parton will also likely be heavily featured in the annual emotional in memoriam segment.
Beyoncé earns her 100th Grammy nomination
Queen Bey made history Monday with her 100th Grammy nomination for best R&B solo performance for her song, “MORNING DEW (DONK).”
Beyoncé has won 35 Grammys in her storied career — the most of any female artist.
Taylor Swift’s recognized for ‘Showgirl’ and ‘Toy Story’
Yes, Swift’s 12th album, “The Life of a Showgirl” came out over a year ago, and yes it still earned several nominations Monday morning.

“Showgirl” took a spot in two of the three top categories, with lead single “The Fate of Ophelia,” earning a place for record of the year, and the album making the list of potential album of the year winners — an award Swift has won more than any other artist in her 20-year career.
“Showgirl” also nabbed nominations for best remixed recording of “Opalite,” and for best pop duo/group performance for song “The Life of a Showgirl,” which features Sabrina Carpenter.
The album, however, did not rise to a nomination for best pop vocal album.
Swift also got two nominations for her single “I Knew It I Knew You,” which she wrote for “Toy Story 5” and released in June — including song of the year.
Swift on Monday tied for the most song of the year nominations, with nine total throughout her career, including hits like “You Belong With Me,” “Blank Space” and “Anti-Hero.”
Madonna makes a comeback
Madonna received her first nominations in 16 years, since 2010, with “Bring Your Love.”
The pop icon, 68, has won 7 Grammy Awards in her decades-long career.
This year marked a comeback for the artist, who also performed at the MTV Video Music Awards for the first time in 23 years. There, she also took home three awards, including artist of the year.
Oscar buzz starts now
The best score soundtrack for visual media (includes film and TV) is typically stacked with Oscar contenders. This year was no different.
Six-time Grammy-winning composer Ludwig Göransson scored two more nods Monday, for his work on two films: “The Odyssey” and “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.”
Göransson has won three Oscars and is expected to be nominated again at Hollywood’s biggest night.
Universal’s “The Odyssey,” which kicked off its Oscar campaign last week, is an expected front-runner in several categories for the Academy Awards.

Daniel Pemberton’s “Project Hail Mary” score was also recognized. The Amazon MGM Studios film, which stars Ryan Gosling, is also among the buzzy Oscar contenders. The Grammy nomination marks a first for Pemberton.
The score for “One Battle After Another,” from composer Jonny Greenwood, was also in the mix of this year’s nominees. The film won six Oscars at the 2026 Oscars.

Swift’s “Toy Story” single, which received Recording Academy recognition, is also expected to be nominated at the Oscars next year. The pop star has already been busy campaigning for the song, with the Grammy nominations now helping fuel her to the top of the contender list.

title: NFL Week 10: A San Francisco score fest and two big injuries
summary: Week 10 of the NFL season featured a San Francisco score fest, a costly clash in Germany and three quarterbacks making their first career starts.
story: Week 10 of the NFL season featured a San Francisco score fest, a costly clash in Germany and three quarterbacks making their first career starts.
Here’s everything you need to know from Sunday.
Can anyone stop the 49ers?
On paper, the sieve-like Dallas Cowboys defense going up against the San Francisco 49ers’ offense looked like a mismatch.
On the field, it played out the same way — although the Cowboys kept it interesting by scoring plenty themselves.

San Francisco improved to 8-1 on the season with the 46-40 road victory, in which Kyle Shanahan’s offense ran 62 plays and gained 584 yards. That average of 9.4 yards per play was the highest of any offense of the last two years, according to NFL research. And that’s even counting the five sacks the 49ers took for a loss of 19 yards. Three touchdowns went for 66 yards or longer.

Could Brock Purdy be building a case for MVP? With three more touchdowns Sunday, he now has 22 touchdowns against five turnovers this season, all while missing multiple teammates on offense due to injuries. For his career, Purdy is 4-0 against Dallas, with nine touchdowns against zero turnovers. He also threw a downfield block to aid a long touchdown run.
The Cowboys (4-6) have now allowed 20-plus points in 17 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. They continue to trail the New York Giants in the NFC East.
Big injuries for the Lions and Patriots
The Lions got Sunday started with a 35-10 win over the Pats in Germany, but the blowout was marred by key injuries for both sides.
New England quarterback Drake Maye left in the first quarter with an ankle injury after he was sacked by Detroit defensive end Aidan Hutchinson — who also hurt himself on the same play.

Hutchinson leapt in celebration after the sack, and his right knee buckled as he hit the turf. Both injuries are believed to be “significant,” NFL Network reports, raising question marks about two teams with Super Bowl aspirations.
Another Browns win, another Deshaun Watson comeback

The Browns improved to 6-4 Sunday, as quarterback Deshaun Watson led yet another last-minute win. In each of Cleveland’s six wins this season, Watson has led a game-winning drive, including four fourth-quarter comebacks.

The Texans led 17-0 in this one, only for the Browns to finish the game on a 27-7 run. Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards, with no touchdowns and one interception. He owes a debt of gratitude to his defense, which held Houston to a whopping six three-and-outs in the second half.

Watson led a short, three-play drive to put Cleveland ahead with under a minute to go. The biggest play of the game was a 30-yard connection between Watson and tight end Harold Fannin Jr., which set up the go-ahead touchdown run by Quinshon Judkins.
With the win, the Browns are now 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963 and remain very much in the hunt in the AFC North.
Bengals win critical AFC North matchup

The Browns weren’t the only big winners in their division Sunday. The NFC North has earned headlines all season because of how difficult the competition is, but don’t overlook the competition taking place in the AFC North, too.

Cincinnati’s 38-18 win on “Sunday Night Football” improved it to 7-2 while dropping Pittsburgh to 6-3. Cleveland is lurking, at 6-4, while Baltimore is 4-5. The win was critical for the Bengals because they had already lost once to the Steelers, in Week 3.

And the 49ers’ Purdy has competition in the MVP debate, because Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is on an historic tear after throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns. He has now scored four or more touchdowns in five consecutive games, tied with Peyton Manning in 2004 for the longest streak in NFL history.
Speaking of Burrow, how ridiculous was it that 231 of his passing yards went to star receiver Ja’Marr Chase alone? The eight Steelers who caught a pass Sunday combined for 143 receiving yards total.
Mahomes moves past Manning
The record set Sunday by Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes was a decade in the making.

Mahomes threw five touchdown passes in a 35-13 Chiefs (7-2) win over Atlanta (3-7) and now has thrown for more touchdown passes than any quarterback in NFL history through their first 10 seasons. That record had belonged to Peyton Manning, with 327.

Mahomes entered Sunday tied with Manning’s mark, before quickly passing it during a game in which he lit up the Falcons even though running back Kenneth Walker Jr. didn’t play (groin) and tight end Travis Kelce injured his right ankle early in the opening quarter.
This was the record-setting throw:
It was Mahomes’ first five-touchdown game since Week 1 of 2022.
Somebody has to win the NFC South

The Panthers beat the Saints 20-17 on a walk-off field goal in New Orleans. Carolina is 4-5 after the victory…and in sole possession of first place in the NFC South. The Panthers won the division last year with a losing record of 8-9.
QB carousel
If you’ve had the feeling you’ve seen more quarterbacks play this season than is typical, your instinct is correct.

With No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza taking over in Las Vegas, Carson Beck starting in Arizona and Kyle McCord starting Sunday for Miami, it marked only the second time in the last 15 years that 50 or more quarterbacks had started a game through Week 10 (with 2019 being the other instance).

Mendoza started strong but ultimately struggled against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks. He ran for a touchdown on the Raiders’ opening drive, but he finished the game with only 143 yards on 17-of-29 passing in a 21-13 loss. Mendoza was also sacked six times, though he did pick up 22 yards on the ground. Since the 1970 merger, quarterbacks selected No. 1 overall have now gone 5-24-1 in their first career start.
Beck had a rough day, completing 11 of 18 throws for 108 yards. He was picked off twice and sacked five times in a 34-6 defeat to the Rams.

McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards in a 24-22 Dolphins loss to Indianapolis. The only Dolphins passing touchdown of the day, however, was thrown by receiver Malik Washington as part of a trick play.
Trade deadline’s big move pays dividends
Making his first start for the Vikings since 2023, Kirk Cousins led Minnesota to a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

Cousins was acquired just five days prior from the Las Vegas Raiders, and he combined with another dominant Vikings defensive display to end Minnesota’s two-game losing streak and improve the team’s record to 7-2.

The performance made clear why so many tipped the Vikings as contenders if they could only marry their defensive prowess with competent quarterback play. The Vikings are now two games clear of Green Bay, keeping pace with Detroit and the Chicago Bears in the loaded NFC North.
Aaron Donald earns first sack in 1,050 days

Since he unretired and rejoined the Rams before the season, Aaron Donald had yet to truly look like the three-time former NFL defensive player of the year. Sure, the defensive lineman had affected opposing offenses in hard-to-measure ways by forcing them to account for him, but he’d yet to record a sack.
Until Sunday.
In his eighth game of his return, Donald sacked Beck, the Arizona rookie, to record his first sack in 1,050 days.

He added to his total later with a half-sack. The Rams (6-4) won their fourth straight game by smothering the Cardinals (3-7) all game in a 34-6 win so lopsided the Rams ran more than twice as many plays. It marked Arizona’s franchise-record 11th consecutive loss at home.

title: Flight delays and cancellations return to normal levels after weekend of travel chaos
summary: Air travel across the United States was largely returning to normal Monday, although some disruption persisted as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule after a rare nationwide ground stop.
story: Air travel across the United States was largely returning to normal Monday, although some disruption persisted as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule after a rare nationwide ground stop.

The extraordinary shutdown saw thousands of fed up passengers stranded, some sleeping in terminals and missing meetings and family occasions. The fallout from Friday’s stoppage was still being felt, with officials blaming a router issue that derailed air traffic control communications.

But by 9 a.m. ET Monday, about 1,500 flights into and out of the U.S. were delayed and nearly 300 canceled, a dramatic drop from the 10,987 delayed and 2,336 canceled U.S. flights Sunday, according to the aviation data site FlightAware.

American Airlines had the largest number of canceled flights Monday at 157, followed by SkyWest with 38 flights. Dallas-Fort Worth International and Chicago O’Hare International were the origin airports experiencing the highest number of cancellations  Monday, according to data from FlightAware.
However, the outlook for the coming days is set to improve with just 3 U.S. flights due to be canceled Tuesday, as passengers gear up for busy Thanksgiving travel later this month.

“It takes some time for the airlines to rechoreograph all of their crews and aircraft. We’re going to start seeing things get better today, but I think back to normal tomorrow,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday.
The nationwide ground stop lasted several hours Friday and stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers across the country.

The Federal Aviation Administration lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday. It was the longest nationwide halt to U.S. air travel since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the United States. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said authorities had found no evidence of a cyberattack.

Duffy on Sunday declined to apologize for the ground stop, instead blaming his predecessors and previous presidential administrations that he said did not do enough to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system.

“It happened on my watch, but we have to be clear: I am moving at an incredible speed that no one has done at the FAA or in decades,” Duffy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press.” “But I can’t apologize for what was passed off to us, and I can’t blame Republicans or Democrats because it’s all of them.”

FAA contractor L3Harris had been working on replacing a copper line with a fiber line at a remote site in El Dorado, Arkansas. Duffy said Sunday that the replacement triggered problems with another recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas, which started broadcasting and overloading routers at other air traffic control centers across the country.
The FAA said it still does not know what ultimately caused the problem that occurred with maintenance work that had been done thousands of times ​before without issue, Duffy added.

Copper-to-fiber optic telecommunications conversions are being completed at FAA facilities around the country at a rapid pace. More than 3,500 communication lines have been replaced out of the 5,170 slated to be switched out by 2028, according to FAA data.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the surge overwhelmed routers at one center and then spread to backup routers at other locations. He said the FAA halted departures to relieve pressure on the system while officials worked to identify the source of the problem.
“I think that was the right call,” Bedford said. “We stand behind that.” Officials are investigating why the router behaved that way.

Friday’s disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a U.S. air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.

President Donald Trump on Sunday called for additional funding from lawmakers, while senior Democrats were skeptical of pleas for more money, pointing to unspent funds. Duffy said that the money unspent last year was earmarked only for certain spending, and did not include funds for new software to manage the airspace.

How I picked the best slow cookers
Here are all the factors and features I considered when making this roundup of slow cooker and multicooking appliances:

Features, modes and settings: For the most part, all slow cookers have the baseline functions low, high and keep warm, which is the case for the appliances on this list. With that said, some slow cookers have additional features like a timer and customized cooking settings based on meat and poultry type as well as amount. Plus, a few of the appliances on this list have sear and saute functions which prevent you from having to do any work on a skillet before adding food to the slow cooker. For the list above, I made sure to include appliances with all traditional slow cooker functions, but I also included a few (from Ninja and Our Place, for example), that have additional settings for more multidimensional cooking at home. Size: Common sizes for slow cookers and multicookers range from two  to around 8.5 quarts. In the list above, I included appliances that fall within this range and emphasize the benefits of having slow cookers in different sizes and capacities, because each one is great for making different courses of meals or food types, like appetizers and side dishes. All of the slow cooker inserts and their corresponding lids on the list above, except one, are dishwasher safe according to their brands. Most of the slow cooker inserts are made from dishwasher-safe stoneware and have glass lids (some of which the brands recommend washing on the top rack, which I noted above). How to shop for a slow cooker
Here are a few things to keep in mind when shopping for a slow cooker. You may benefit from having multiple slow cookers for different purposes and occasions.
Decide on the size

If you live alone and/or don’t do a ton of meal prep, a slow cooker around 2 to 3 quarts may suffice. If you have a large family that you cook for and/or you rely on a slow cooker to meal prep lunches and dinners, a large capacity appliance is the best way to go. Just keep in mind that if you have a small dishwasher, some inserts may be hard to fit in it, in which case, you may need to wash them by hand.
Determine which functions are most important

As the roundup above shows, slow cookers have a wide range of features, modes and settings. If you prefer and only want appliances with the usual high, low and keep warm functions, then there’s no need to get a more complex one like the Ninja Possible Cooker. But if you like being able to make many if not most of your meals in the same appliance, then a slow cooker with several functions, like the Instant Pot, for example, are great options.
Consider portability and cleaning

If you attend a lot of dinner parties and bring food in your slow cooker, then you should consider buying one with a locking lid, which prevents food from leaking or spilling. Plus, some slow cooker inserts are ceramic while others are made from nonstick aluminum, which, depending on what you cook in them, can be harder to clean, so if it isn’t dishwasher safe, this is something to keep in mind.
Frequently asked questions

A Crock Pot and a slow cooker aren’t different appliances — Crock Pot is the brand name for a very popular line of slow cooker appliances. Many people use the term Crock Pot to refer to any slow cooker itself due to the brand’s prevalence and because it helped popularize the appliance.

title: Richard Sterban, distinctive bass vocalist of The Oak Ridge Boys, dies at 83
summary: Richard Sterban, a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley and the inimitable bass singer for The Oak Ridge Boys on their hit “Elvira,” died Saturday.
story: Richard Sterban, a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley and the inimitable bass singer for The Oak Ridge Boys, died Saturday from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia after a battle with cancer.
He was 83.

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers,” his family said in a statement. “Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus.”
Sterban joined The Oak Ridge Boys in 1972 after leaving his job as Elvis Presley’s backup vocalist, a press release states, citing Sterban’s desire to “be in the best vocal group in the world.”
Fellow member of The Oak Ridge Boys, William Lee Golden, said Sterban’s death was a “sad day.”
“GOD Bless and Comfort his Family through this Valley of Sorrow Rest in Peace my Friend,” he wrote on Facebook.

The group won five Grammy Awards and four Academy of Country Music Awards, including Top Vocal Group and Album of the Year, and the prestigious Cliffie Stone Pioneer Award in 2008. It was inducted into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame in 2000 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015.
The Academy of Country Music said Sterban “helped shape one of country music’s most recognizable sounds” and said it was saddened by his death.

“I grew up in radio hearing Richard’s voice come out of every speaker in America. That ‘oom-pa-pa-mow-mow’ on ‘Elvira’ was pure joy,” Academy of Country Music CEO Andy Schuon said in a statement. “He was a gentleman and a believer who carried gospel into country and pop, and brought millions of fans along with him.”

Sterban, born on April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, developed his love for music at a young age. He started singing at 6 years old as a soprano in a Sunday school and as a tenor in his seventh-grade glee club. By the time he started eighth grade, his voice had dropped to bass.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
After graduating from Collingswood High School, Sterban studied music at Trenton State College, now The College of New Jersey.
Sterban helped found the Keystones, a gospel quartet that tenor Joe Bonsall sang in. Bonsall was also a member of The Oak Ridge Boys. He died in 2024.

Sterban’s path led him to sing in the Stamps Quartet, which Presley had hired to sing behind him. He performed with Presley for about a year and a half, until The Oak Ridge Boys called, in need of a bass singer. Sterban joined the group, replacing Noel Fox.

Johnny Cash featured the group in his touring show and helped them sign to Columbia Records in 1973, but success did not come overnight, and their two albums drew little notice. While performing, the group caught the attention of music manager Jim Halsey, who convinced them to try country music. They later signed with Halsey, making hit after hit. “Y’all Come Back Saloon” reached No. 3 on the country chart in 1977 and “I’ll Be True to You” climbed to No. 1, the press release states.

In 1981, the group released “Elvira,” which also hit No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart, sold more than two million copies, was named Single of the Year by both the Country Music Association and the Academy of Country Music, and won a Grammy Award.
The group also performed for four presidents, from Gerald Ford to George W. Bush.
Sterban is survived by his wife, Donna, and his five children.

title: When J. Lo Joked About Her 4 Divorces, a Fan’s Witty Response Left Her Cackling: ‘Funniest Thing I Ever Heard’
summary: Jennifer Lopez laughed when a fan made a joke about her four divorces. Hear the line that cracked her up.
story: When it comes to the highs and lows of her very public love life, Jennifer Lopez has a sense of humor.
Over the weekend, the  “Ain’t It Funny” singer spoke to fans at a screening of her new TV special, “The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas,” at the 92nd Street Y in New York.
She said her four divorces are a “big part of my story.” The singer then said, “Four times,” and held up four fingers.
When a fan in the audience shouted, “You have six more fingers!” Lopez couldn’t help but laugh, per a video captured at the event.
“Yes I do!” she said as she excitedly tapped her feet on the floor and pointed into the crowd.
Lopez was clearly impressed with the witty comment and said, “Oh my God, that is the funniest thing I’ve ever heard in my life.”
Someone on the stage also acknowledged that the clever phrase has potential.
“That’s a T-shirt,” they said, prompting Lopez to agree.
In a video clip of the moment, the crowd erupted in laughter over the comedic exchange. Social media users also got a good giggle.
“You know its funny when you laugh and stomp at the same time,” one commented.
“Collect those rings,” another wrote.
One Instagram user said, “I’d buy that tshirt too!!!” and another embraced Lopez’s honesty, writing, “Right! Live your life.”
Marina Prut, the content creator who captured the video, called Lopez an “inspiration.”
“If she can work this hard, reaching new heights, fall and rise again — so can we,” she tells TODAY.com.

Lopez has been married four times. First to Ojani Noa for a year from 1997 to 1998, then Cris Judd from 2001 to 2003. She has twins with her third husband, Marc Anthony, to whom she was married from 2004 to 2014.
She and Ben Affleck, who were previously engaged, married in 2022 and split in 2024.
She was also engaged to Alex Rodriguez; the couple was together from 2017 to 2021.
Lopez poked fun at her weddings in her 2024 music video “Can’t Get Enough.”
During a 2025 interview on the “Howard Stern Show,” she said she felt that she has never been truly loved, but she has loved.

“It’s not that I’m not lovable. It’s that they’re not capable,” she said. “They don’t have it in them. And they gave me what they had, they gave me all of it every time. All the rings, all the things I could ever want. The houses, the rings, the marriage, all of it. But they didn’t love me and I didn’t love myself.”
She said her last divorce was the “best thing that happened to (her).”

title: Robert Pattinson Announced as the New James Bond
summary: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced.
story: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond.

Pattinson will take on the role of film’s most famous British secret agent in the 26th installment of the long-running Bond franchise. The upcoming movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the mastermind behind the “Dune” trilogy.

Pattinson starred in “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” “Primetime” and “Dune: Part Three” this year alone. He follows in the footsteps of Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, Timothy Dalton, Roger Moore, Sean Connery and George Lazenby, who all played Bond on the big screen.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “... To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”
The announcement comes five years after Craig played the suave spy, whose code name is 007, in the last Bond film, 2021’s “No Time to Die.”
Casting rumors about the new Bond have been making headlines for months.

In October, Deadline reported that several A-list British actors were performing screen tests for the coveted role. Insiders told the publication that top contenders at that time were “One Night Only” star Callum Turner, “Slow Horses” and “White Lotus” actor Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor of “The Crown” and “Challengers.”
Weeks later, Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were suddenly in the running, according to Variety.
Pop star Harry Styles also engaged in “discussions” about the part, Variety reported.
The Bond character was created in 1952 by British author Ian Fleming, who wrote about the secret agent across 12 novels and two short story collections.
Brosnan, who played Bond from 1995 until 2002, told Vanity Fair he would be pleased to see Turner, his co-star in 2017’s “The Only Living Boy in New York,” take on the role.

“All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men,” Brosnan said.
“Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage,” Brosnan added.

title: The Most Important Line in ‘The Good Daughter,’ According to Karin Slaughter, Is ‘Not a Message Women Get Often’
summary: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “The Good Daughter.”
story: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “The Good Daughter.”

From the moment two masked men with guns step into the home of teenage sisters Samantha and Charlotte Quinn, it’s clear that crime drama “The Good Daughter” is a story about survival — what happens after violence changes the trajectory of your life, and the pain of piecing together your past.
It’s just one of several traumatic plot points in the six-episode series, based on the book of the same name by bestselling author Karin Slaughter, out Nov. 12 on Peacock.
While sexual violence is a theme in much of Slaughter’s work, extra care was given to how this story was brought to the small screen, Slaughter tells TODAY.com.

“One of the things I’m most proud of in this show is I set these rules that we were only going to tell the story from the perspective of Sam or Charlie,” she says. “If it’s young Charlie, (director Steph Green) would lower the camera angle, and the focus is always on the girls and not on the bad men doing bad things.”

“I’m very mindful that when you see a woman’s body, you think about how you feel, and when you see a man’s body, you think about how the man feels. So I wanted to really make sure that we weren’t being exploitative and we were showing this perspective.”

“The Good Daughter” revolves around the sisters Charlotte “Charlie” and Samantha “Sam,” played by Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne respectively, who are estranged as adults but reunite after one of them becomes unintentionally linked to a murder case. Together, the siblings must contend with the past in order to reconcile and embrace their futures.
Both Byrne and Fahy tell TODAY.com that they were drawn to the project because of the show’s focus on the strength of the characters, rather than on the abuse and suffering that they had endured.

“The show is about hope, and it’s about perseverance, and it’s about confronting the things that scare you, relieving yourself of unnecessary shame, and claiming the life that you really want to have for yourself and the people that you love,” Fahy says.

Byrne adds: “We wanted to celebrate the resilience of all situations like that and all people who survived these horrific events. ... A huge part of the conversation around when I signed on (was) how will this be dealt with? How will this be depicted?”

Both actors were tasked with embodying survivorship in different ways. For Byrne, Sam’s disability from a bullet wound to the head meant two months working on her gait with a physical therapist who rehabilitates similar patients in real life.
Fahy’s character Charlie, meanwhile, has kept a secret about the attack from everyone except her father, Rusty. Asked how she was able to bring that to life, Fahy points to the “responsibly run set.”

“There was a mental health specialist on set every day that was available to all of the actors and all of the crew if anybody needed support,” Fahy says, adding that Green “took very good care of everybody, so that created a super safe space.”
Slaughter hopes the show helps viewers, particularly those who have gone through trauma of their own, feel supported and safe.

“The most important line in the entire series and in the book is when Rusty says, ‘Whatever you did to survive is exactly what you should do,’” Slaughter explains. “That’s not a message women get often. We aren’t usually told, ‘You did the right thing.’ We’re told, ‘Why didn’t you do this? Why didn’t you do that?’”

On its face, “The Good Daughter” may seem like a quintessential thriller about women solving a crime in a small-town. But, according to Slaughter, it relies just as heavily on other warmer storytelling elements, like comedy and family dynamics.

“It’s so important to me to balance the light and dark,” the author says. “There are laugh-out-loud funny moments ... and that was so important for me to carry from the book into the show because, particularly being from the South ... there is that sensibility of even the worst situation you can find humor in.”
Slaughter adds that connection between the two sisters “propels you through the show as much as the whodunit.”
“At its heart, it’s about a family and this universal sense of dislocation and separation that we all feel as we grow up,” she says.
In fact, the least surprising but perhaps most satisfying aspect of the ending is that Sam and Charlie finally accept how much they need each other.

“The thing about writing about complicated, interesting women and not sentimentalizing them is that you have to know, as a viewer, that you trust the writer (is) going to leave you in a good place, and all my books end on a place of hope, and definitely the show ends on that hope too,” Slaughter says.

title: Has Madeline Miller Seen ‘The Odyssey’ Yet? She Told Jenna
summary: Madeline Miller, author of The Song of Achilles and Circe, shares whether she’s seen Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and why she hasn’t yet
story: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” was practically required viewing for anyone working in the world of Greek mythology. Well, almost anyone.
On the Nov. 12 episode of “Open Book With Jenna,” author Madeline Miller, who is known for her Greek myth retellings, shared that she hasn’t seen the movie (yet).
“I get terrible migraines from large screens,” Miller told Jenna Bush Hager, adding that she’ll be waiting to watch it from the comfort of her home.
“You and I will be the only (ones) to watch it from our home television,” Jenna remarked.
“The Odyssey” has grossed $1.7 billion worldwide. When the movie was released over the summer, fans clamored for tickets for IMAX and 70mm IMAX screenings.
The author said that she’s seen “The Odyssey” through the eyes of friends and family, who report back to her with “all the details.”

“It was actually a total joy to have people reaching out to me and telling me what they thought about it,” Miller said. “I kind of feel like I’ve seen it, but I’ve seen it through the eyes of all the people I love ... it’s the best, honestly.”

Miller’s first book, “The Song of Achilles,” was a retelling of “The Iliad.” Her second, “Circe,” turned a side character of “The Odyssey” into a lead. Circe, played by Samantha Morton, has a pivotal scene in Nolan’s film.
“Circe goes back to my 8th Grade self reading ‘The Odyssey’ for the first time, and being so disappointed in how little page time Circe gets,” Miller said.

She remembers “wanting more” out of the  enchantress’ backstory. “Why is she turning men into pigs? Who is this woman? How did she get that kind of power? What does it mean to be a witch? All of those things had been sitting with me and getting louder and louder in the background,” she said.
After “Song of Achilles” was finished, Miller said it was “so clear” that she had to focus on Circe.
“It was amazing to get to spend seven years living inside Circe’s head,” Miller said.

Her most recent offering is “Mestra,” a novella pulled from Ovid’s “Metamorphoses.” In it, Poseidon grants a young woman incredible powers of shape-shifting, and she uses them, at first, to please her demanding father, and later to free herself from him.
Miller has been struggling with the effects of long COVID and felt she finally had the concentration and energy to work on fiction.
“It feels like this story just exploded out of me. It was such a tremendous joy, even though the story is in many ways unsettling,” she said.

title: Read With Jenna Jr. Is Coming to the Libby App! How to Read the Books — for Free
summary: You’ll soon be able to read Read with Jenna Jr. picks on the Libby app. Here’s how to find them.
story: You’ll soon be able to read Read with Jenna Jr. book picks in the Libby app, making bedtime reading even easier.
In a new partnership, Read with Jenna and The Libby App are joining together to give readers a way to get the latest book club picks at their fingertips.
This year’s Read With Jenna Jr. list had 21 books ranging from young readers through YA.
The Libby App is a free mobile app that lets readers borrow eBooks and audiobooks from their local library.
Upon login, readers will now find Read With Jenna’s curated book list, front and center in the app — an opportunity to read Jenna’s selections for free!
How to find Read With Jenna Jr. books on Libby
It’s easy — all you’ll need is your library card.
Get a library card by applying online or stop by your local branch.
Get on the Libby app from the app store.
Find Read With Jenna books and customized reading guides right on your home screen.
Since 2019, Jenna Bush Hager has chosen a new book for Read With Jenna each month. She started her kid-friendly list in 2023.

Raised by a librarian mom, Jenna loves libraries, which is what makes the partnership so special. “Libraries have always been close to my heart. They’re more than buildings filled with books, they’re community spaces, and gateways to discovery,” she says.
“I hope you’ll join me in celebrating libraries, and finding your next favorite Read with Jenna book with Libby. So grab your library card, get on Libby, and let’s read together.”
What is Libby?
Libby is a free-to-use mobile app built by OverDrive. It’s free to use with a library card and gives you access to thousands of eBooks and audiobooks, including monthly Read with Jenna picks.

story: An all-star group of television legends from Jerry Seinfeld to Mariska Hargitay is set to celebrate NBC’s 100th anniversary in style.

NBC announced the first wave of the star-studded lineup that will be part of “NBC100: The Live Celebration,” a broadcast special airing on Dec. 10 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock in honor of the network’s anniversary.
The list was first shared on TODAY Nov. 16 and features generations of entertainment, news and sports luminaries from NBC’s history.
Among those appearing are Seinfeld, Hargitay, David Letterman, Conan O’Brien, Jimmy Fallon, Larry David, Simone Biles, Tina Fey, Ted Danson, Michael Phelps and more.

The three-hour live event from the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles will celebrate the television characters, comedy legends and athletes who have made NBC part of the fabric of American culture for a century. It will feature musical performances, surprise reunions and flashbacks to iconic NBC moments, plus appearances by stars of classic NBC shows like “ER,” “The Office,” “Parks and Recreation,” “Law & Order,” “30 Rock” and “Saturday Night Live.”
Additional talent, cast reunions, musical performances and special appearances will be announced at a later date.

summary: Michael J. Fox posed with wife and fellow actor Tracy Pollan, along with all three of their daughters, Esmé Annabelle Fox, 25, and twins Schuyler Fox and Aquinnah Kathleen Fox, 31, in a rare appearance together at his annual gala.
story: It’s a family affair!
Actor Michael J. Fox hit the red carpet on Nov. 14 with his family for his foundation’s annual gala, “A Funny Thing Happened On The Way To Cure Parkinson’s” event in New York City.

The 65-year-old posed with wife and fellow actor Tracy Pollan, along with all three of their daughters, Esmé Annabelle Fox, 25, and twins Schuyler Fox and Aquinnah Kathleen Fox, 31, in a rare appearance all together. The couple’s son, Sam Michael Fox, was not in attendance.

Michael J. Fox, who founded the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research in 2000, sported a T-shirt under a more formal jacket. Meanwhile, Pollan and the couple’s daughters rocked stunning gowns for the event.

The night was a particularly eventful one, as it not only featured star-studded attendees from Stephen Colbert and David Letterman to TODAY’s Willie Geist, but also several comedy and musical performances.
Among those to take the stage were John Mayer, Brad Paisley and Michael J. Fox himself, who rocked out on the electric guitar.
Comedians, including Josh Johnson and Tom Papa, also performed sets throughout the night.

Fox has been a vocal proponent of Parkinson’s research. In September, he was awarded the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the Emmys for his philanthropy. In his acceptance speech, Fox offered some hopeful remarks.
“I’m proud of the progress we’ve made to benefit Parkinsons patients, and families,” Fox said in his acceptance speech. “We move closer to eradicating this disease forever.”
Fox, who was diagnosed in 1991, kept the information private for years before opening up about the disease until 1998.
During a 2020 interview with Willie, Fox discussed his journey to accepting the diagnosis.

“You eventually come to a place where you go, ‘I can do this.’ This is just the way it is. It’s something that happened to me. It’s not something I’m suffering from. It’s my reality,” he said. “I find that the partner of gratitude is acceptance and surrender.”

title: Snooki Gifts Internet With ‘The Poof’ Tutorial As the 2000s Hairstyle Makes a Comeback
summary: If there’s one person we can learn from in creating the most authentic 2000s hair poof, it’s the “Jersey Shore” queen herself, Snooki.
story: If there’s one person we can learn from in creating the most authentic 2000s hair poof, it’s the “Jersey Shore” queen herself, Snooki.
Snooki, whose real name is Nicole Polizzi, took to social media to share a tutorial for the iconic hairstyle that she so famously rocked on the MTV reality show.
The video, posted Nov. 14, comes as the millennial hair trend has been revived by younger generations across social media. And Snooki just had to show the youth how it’s done.
“I’ve been summoned by a lot of you talking about a trend that might be coming back — a hair trend, if you will — from the younger generation,” Snooki says in the video.
She adds: “We’re talking about ‘the poof.’”
And fans were unsurprisingly delighted by the tutorial from the Queen of Poofs.
“it’s like watching the Mona Lisa being painted,” a TikTok user wrote.
Another person wrote on TikTok that “Snooki wearing a poof in 2026 has healed something in me 🥰😭🖤”

Snooki, who rose to fame after the premiere of the reality show in the 2009, became known for her peak millennial look that often involved a tan, graphic tanks, heavy black eyeliner, animal prints and, of course, the signature Poof. So, she certainly has the credentials to teach us all a thing or two.

In the video, Snooki starts off, clarifying that the hairstyle should be referred as “The Poof,” rather than “the hair bump.” She also expresses a strong distaste for the “Bumpit,” the iconic hair tool that many millennials used to create the voluminous style. The reality star then explains some other common faux pas that she’s noticed.

“They’re showing themselves doing the hair bump with bobby pins. Bobby pins. Bobby pins! I don’t know what’s happening. What are we doing?” she says in the video. “So I feel like the mother hen needs to come in and say, “Girls, no, no. If we’re gonna bring this back and do it, do it the right way. We have to do it the right way.”
Snooki then dives into her step-by-step instructions to re-create the look. It goes a little something like this:
Tease the Section of Hair That You Plan To Use for the Poof
“For me, I always had thick hair. I never really needed to tease, but obviously, if you got a tease, you tease the s--- out of it,” Snooki says.
This part, she underscores is not to be taken lightly.
“You do it for a long time. OK? A long time,” she says of the teasing.
Grab a Clip — Not a Bobby Pin
After the section of hair is properly teased, gather the section with a hair clip.
“These clips, you get it from Sally’s. They’re 99 cents,” Snooki says. “This is the clip you use. No bobby pins.”
Secure the poof onto your head with the clip.
Hairspray, Duh!
Next comes an essential aspect of the hairstyle: Hairspray.
In the tutorial, Snooki applies hairspray extremely liberally to the poofed section of hair.
Finish It Off by Fanning out the Poof
Fan out the poof so that the strands form a perfect rainbow shape.
“Make it nice and cute, and you can even go bigger,” Snooki says, as she arranges her strands. “I used to go way bigger.”
And there you have it!

title: John Mulaney Sells You an Age-Old Parental Care System, ‘Sister,’ in ‘SNL’ Skit That’s Too Real
summary: Comedian John Mulaney, who hosted the Nov. 14 episode of “Saturday Night Live,” portrayed a salesman who’s promoting a convenient elder care system known as “Sister.” And for many families, this one’s a little too real.
story: This one goes out to all the devoted daughters out there!

Comedian John Mulaney, who hosted the Nov. 14 episode of “Saturday Night Live,” portrayed a salesman who’s promoting a convenient elder care system known as “Sister.” And for many families, this one’s a little too real.
In the “ad,” Mulaney begins by presenting the quintessential dilemma for people who don’t want to turn to outside help to care for aging parents.

“My dad means the world to me. So when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible,” he says. “I didn’t want to put him in a nursing home, but a private health aide could cost thousands a week. I didn’t know where to turn. That’s when I heard about ‘Sister.’”
“Sister,” Mulaney explains, is a free, 24/7 elder care provider who is “also your sister.”

“Now I don’t have to worry about Dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life and the stuff I like to do,” he says. His sister, who is portrayed by Jane Wickline, scrambles to make sure their dad is cared for.
The sketch also features some of the show’s male cast members, raving about the elder care system.
“I love my mom more than anything. That doesn’t mean I want to help her in the bathroom. Sister doesn’t either, but she will. Whereas I won’t,” Andrew Dismukes says. “That’s the sister difference.”
Mikey Day — who plays character Dr. Grant, author of “Not It! A Son’s Guide To Elder Care” — breaks down the system for viewers.

“Here’s how it works. First, years of internalized sexism warps sister’s brain into thinking caretaking is her responsibility and somehow not yours,” Dr. Grant says. “Next, your text arrives, instantly activating her, and that’s it. You’re done for life. See you at the funeral!”
Mulaney concludes the commercial by offering an extra special offer.
“Sign up now, and we’ll throw in sister’s husband, whether he likes it or not,” he says.
Oof.
For many viewers, the dark humor sketch was just way too honest.
“I was Sister. This sketch was too accurate,” one person wrote in the comments on YouTube.
Another person wrote that they were “laughing so hard because this hit WAY too close to home!”
“SNL, I did NOT give you permission to turn my family drama into a skit!” the social media user said.

The Nov. 14 show marked Mulaney’s seventh time hosting. The former “SNL” writer’s big night was well-received and included several major highlights like former cast member Bowen Yang’s return to the Studio 8H stage.

title: Bowen Yang Makes Electric Return to ‘SNL’ As Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang
summary: Bowen Yang surprised audiences on Nov. 14 with an electrifying appearance on the latest episode of “Saturday Night Live.” Yang, who departed the sketch comedy show in 2025, returned during the cold open to play disgraced ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
story: He’s back like he never left!

Former cast member Bowen Yang surprised audiences on Nov. 14 with an electrifying appearance on the latest episode of “Saturday Night Live.” Yang, who departed the sketch comedy show in 2025, returned during the cold open to play disgraced ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Yang, sporting gray hair and a leather jacket, performed a hilarious spoof of the tech billionaire.
“It’s me, Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang,” Yang says. “Ladies, when you invite Jensen over, you know what’s about to go down — the S&P 500.”

In the skit, host John Mulaney plays a CIA official who gathers the nation’s most prominent tech billionaires, from Elon Musk to Sam Altman, for a training on how to distinguish between a spy and a woman who’s actually interested in them.
Mulaney, referencing Huang’s scandal, asks the group, “What do you think the lesson is here?”
Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg, played by cast member Andrew Dismukes, responds, “Never date a human woman.”
Mulaney really attempts to get his point across, at one point resorting to some visual aids.

“Now I know you dorks like charts, so let’s take a look at this Venn diagram,” Mulaney says while pointing to a graphic on a screen. “On this side we have beautiful women, and on this side we have people who would be interested in your shared opinions and interests. I cannot stress this enough. There is no overlap.”
As Mulaney attempts to inform the clueless tech bosses, with little avail, he decides to pivot to a different strategy.
“Maybe what would help is if I hand it over to someone who learned this lesson the hard way,” Mulaney says, before Yang walks into the room.
“Fellas, don’t be like me,” “Jensen” says, delivering his cautionary tale. “Remember, women don’t like guys like us. That’s how we became guys like us.”

The cold open isn’t the only appearance Yang made in the show. He also made another cameo as Mary Todd Lincoln in “Little Park of Horrors,” a musical sketch in which Mulaney plays a sad horse carriage operator who’s lamenting the recent horse-drawn carriage ban in New York City.

Yang, who is currently playing Mary Todd Lincoln in the hit Broadway play “Oh, Mary!,” steps in to sing a parody of “And I’m Telling You I’m Not Going” from “Dreamgirls” about a ride through the Lincoln Tunnel.
