Yang left “SNL” midway through his eight season on the show. During his time on the sketch comedy show, Yang became a major breakout star, with some of his most memorable roles being his impression of viral pygmy hippo Moo Deng and the iceberg that sank the Titanic.

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Season 11 Star Rob Feeley Unpacks ‘Tough to Watch’ Moments and Where He and Michaella Stand Now
summary: Rob Feeley is ready to unpack his tumultuous season of “Love Is Blind.” He opens up to TODAY.com about his relationship with Michaella Giorgio.
story: Rob Feeley is ready to unpack his tumultuous season of “Love Is Blind.”

The 40 year old, who works in AI infrastructure sales, was highlighted early on in Season 11 of the Netflix dating show for his rowdy personality. His demeanor was one of the many reasons Michaella Giorgio fell for him in the pods. The two got engaged and developed a stronger connection during their couples’ trip to Mexico.

Back in Boston, they met each other’s families and seemed poised to become a “Love Is Blind” success story. But their relationship took a drastic turn when Giorgio was introduced to Feeley’s friends, with some fans calling out Feeley and the men for how they treated Giorgio during the interaction. The next day, Feeley spiraled at a cast meetup and he and Michaella later broke up.
“I think looking back, 100% I should have stepped in and hindsight’s 20/20,” he tells TODAY.com after watching the awkward exchange between his friend group and Giorgio.
He adds that he and the one particular friend who rubbed some viewers the wrong way “had a serious conversation after watching that whole thing.”
“It was not a good situation. It was really tough to watch,” he shares.

Below, he opens up more about the unraveling of his relationship with Giorgio, including conversations the two had after they exited the experiment. He also reveals details about the lifestyle changes he made following the show and why he adjusted his stance on therapy.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
I mean, some ups and some downs. But overall, it’s been OK.

I think looking back, 100% I should have stepped in. Hindsight’s 20/20. But looking at it on camera, which I didn’t have the opportunity, there were a lot of situations that I wish I could have taken back, and especially my friend. My friend and I had a serious conversation after watching that whole thing. It was not a good situation. It was really tough to watch.

If there’s anyone that is embarrassed about that whole situation, it’s my friend. He was not in a good place post that conversation, in regards to seeing it back. Obviously, I think we can all agree he was a little bit intoxicated. It’s not a secret, and I think that if there’s anyone who is regretful and really, really sad about that situation, it’s him. He’s very, very apologetic to Michaella and the whole situation, and if he could take it back, he would every second of the day.

I can’t control the questions my friends ask. I think my friends protect me just like anyone’s friends. So I think that we just wanted to make sure that everyone’s there for the right reasons. I don’t think there was any malintent in asking those questions. I asked Morrey Eglin that question actually. I’m like, “What are you here for?” There was no agenda behind that. I think that everyone just kind of is wondering, like, “What’s going on? Who’s here for the right intentions?” But that’s not indicative to who Michaella is. I don’t think she was here for the wrong intentions, obviously. You can clearly see post-show she’s not here for the wrong intentions.
I’m not really sure. I think I just wanted to trust the process, and I feel like I just want to keep going through the process.

I can’t really recall in terms of that. Diana and I had a great relationship in the pods. She’s awesome. She’s amazing. I don’t really know. I don’t really recall in regards to, like, the canceling thing. I said it a few times. I don’t really know to be honest.

I didn’t really have many concerns. I think I just was there to just find my person, and at the end of the day, I wish I did and unfortunately I didn’t. I didn’t really have a ton of concerns. You know, it’s “Love Is Blind,” and I’d never watched the show in my entire life. I went on legit to find love.

Because I was 38 years old at the time, I wanted to find my person, and I felt like it was a very cool way to find your person, and not just have to look at the exterior. Have that person’s soul, that person’s heart, that person’s personality mean more to you than what they look like on the outside.

My friends were, like, because they obviously knew I was looking for love. I was in my late 30s. They’re just like, “Hey, I think this’d be a good idea because you’re at that position in your life where you’re looking for your forever person. You’re going to take it very seriously. Like, you’re not someone who’s going to go on here to not take it seriously.” They’re like, “Throw your name in the hat.”
I just think I was overwhelmed overall. I think Michaela deserved way better. So at that time, I was like, “You know what, you deserve better.” That’s pretty much it.

I think there wasn’t really an overall like one-on-one, we’re going to end it now. I think that at that moment at Lansdowne (Pub), I guess she ended it. Then I went for my exit interview, and I was informed that she ended it. So, yeah, that was kind of it.
I think everyone was hurt.

No, so we talked right after my exit interview. We spoke. We hung out post the breakup, and then we just would (stay) in touch. Then eventually, she’s like, “Hey, Rob, I don’t think I can stay in communication anymore. You know, it’s not easy for me.” I said, “OK, no problem,” and that was it. So I respect a person’s boundaries. I wanted to stay cordial, but she said, “Hey, it’s not easy for me to just talk to you and be your friend.” I said, “OK, no worries. I respect your decision.”

Not too sure. We were supposed to be season 10, and then I think I reached out. We had a lot of conversations. I think I reached out. I was like, “Hey, how do you feel about this?” And then she’s like, “Hey, it’s not easy for me to speak to you and I need to move on.” I said, “No problem.” That was it.

Of course. It wasn’t just 50 days. It was 75 after that. It’s my whole lifestyle. But I felt like I needed to take a moment to myself, or 50 days to myself, and just reflect, work on myself. Anyone that knows me knows this. It was a very intense experience for me, and I did not do this for the clout. I was just working on myself and being by myself for a lot of that time … being with my family, my close friends, and I didn’t really want to be in the outside world.

I think that I just looked at it in a different perspective. I was like, “You know what? Maybe this can work.” Because I had been to therapy, like when I was young. So I just think that I needed to talk to somebody about my whole experience. Not just my experience on “Love Is Blind,” but just in life.

I would say that maybe it was a little bit of an eye opener. But again, you don’t know my life, and a lot of people don’t. But those 15 days were very tough in regards to, like, I don’t want to ever hurt somebody. What I’ve been through, and things in my past, like, that’s why on the show I didn’t really dive into it because I made a promise to myself and my family I wasn’t going to dive into certain things that (are) personal. So I didn’t want to dive into all those things if that makes sense. But I did think after the show in certain moments, I had to reflect. I’m like, “S---. I should probably talk to somebody.”
I think, again, for me, it was just the pressure. It was a lot, and I feel like you know when you hurt somebody, it’s not easy to come back. So, yeah, I think his assessment was fairly right.

I would say I learned a lot about myself, and if I could do things differently, I would have. And don’t let the emotion get the best of you. I probably should have communicated better early in the process.

title: Lucille Ball Reminisces About ‘I Love Lucy’ In 1983 TODAY Interview
summary: Lucille Ball talked to TODAY in 1983 about what it took to create “I Love Lucy” and how she overcame obstacles to do so.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Lucille Ball talking about the legacy of “I Love Lucy” on Feb. 16, 1983.
“I Love Lucy” was an American institution when star Lucille Ball sat down with Jane Pauley to look back at the pioneering sitcom on Feb. 16, 1983.

“I Love Lucy” premiered Oct. 15, 1951 — nearly three months to the day before TODAY would first sign on — and ran for six seasons, living on for decades beyond that in syndication. It chronicled a middle-class wife (Ball), who often gets involved in hairbrained schemes, much to the chagrin of her husband, played by Ball’s real-life husband, Desi Arnaz.
As Ball, who died in 1989, told Pauley, though, the show almost never got off the ground.
Did Lucille Ball Think She Was a Trailblazer?
“I Love Lucy” remains one of the most beloved shows ever, but Ball didn’t consider the idea that she was some sort of visionary.
“No ... I was only going to work for about a year, a year or two, so that I had something like home movies to show my baby. I was pregnant at the time,” she said.
Her daughter, Lucie, was born in 1951, and her son, Desi Jr., would be born in 1953, with the pregnancy famously being written into the show.
CBS wanted Ball and her husband to come up with an idea for a show. However, the network didn’t want him involved, also insisting the show shoot in New York.

“I stuck to my guns,” Ball said. “I said, ‘I certainly don’t want to quit pictures and do television and have to move to New York. That doesn’t make sense. I want to stay home and have babies, and that’s why we want to work together.’ And they said, ‘Well, it didn’t seem quite right to have a Cuban husband for a young American couple.’ I said, ‘Why not? We are married.’ Well, they still didn’t buy it.”
“You gotta admit, it does sound like an odd pairing, doesn’t it?” Pauley asked.
“And it was,” Ball shot back, with a laugh.
Ball and Arnaz had no interest in shooting in New York. So when CBS threatened to drop the show, Ball said she and Arnaz “scraped together $5,000” which helped them gain ownership of it.
How About Those Co-Stars?!
“I Love Lucy” was enhanced by the presence of Vivian Vance and William Frawley, who played married couple Ethel and Fred Mertz, respectively.
“We had an idea of what we wanted and they were available. They were there at the right time, the right place, and thank God we found them,” Ball said.
“It was a very, very close, well-knit marriage of two married generations, the older marrieds and the younger marrieds,” she said, “and that was what made it so marvelous to play the satire against.”
How Did Lucille Ball Approach the Show?

Calling herself a connoisseur of the show, Pauley admitted she could probably do some routines from it. This prompted Ball to ask if she could “Vitameatavegamin,” a reference to the famous episode where Lucy gets a job in a commercial for a tonic that, unbeknownst to her, has a lot of alcohol in it.
Pauley then tried to pronounce Vitameatavegamin, with help from Ball.
Before their sit down ended, the comedy icon reflected on audience reception to her show.

“A lot of people don’t love Lucy, especially when they’re working, they don’t think of it that way,” she said, before stressing the grueling schedule. “But I had a show to get on, and we had our timing down a certain way.

“We had to accomplish a lot of things by a certain time, and if I hadn’t accomplished them, I knew that I was way behind,” she explained, “because we did our show from 10 o’clock Monday morning and we did it in front of an audience at 3 o’clock Thursday afternoon.”
She added, “And every minute counted.”

title: Jenna Dewan Addresses Shocking ‘DWTS’ Exit, Partner Val Chmerkovskiy’s Brief Suspension
summary: Actor Jenna Dewan just opened up in a recent interview about her elimination from “Dancing With the Stars,” after weeks dominating the reality competition show’s leaderboard.
story: Actor Jenna Dewan just opened up in a recent interview about her elimination from “Dancing With the Stars,” after weeks dominating the reality competition show’s leaderboard.

Dewan, who exited the show after the latest Grammy Night-themed episode, spoke to Women’s Health about her run on the competition, the mid-season controversy involving her dance partner, pro Val Chmerkovskiy, and her departure. She told the outlet that she’s feeling “all kinds of things” but is “mostly proud.”

“I feel really proud of myself, and I feel proud of the last dance we gave on the ballroom floor, and I feel obviously sad that it’s over, that I don’t get to give any more dances out there and create any more special pieces,” Dewan told the outlet. “So I think it’s really both. I feel really proud of us, and I feel fulfilled, and I feel filled up, and I also feel sad that the journey of creating dances is over.”
Dewan called the journey an “enormous undertaking, and it’s  physically, emotionally, mentally, spiritually intense.”
“And so, when that’s just finished, it’s like a light switch goes off, and then you almost don’t even know where you are,” she said.

Dewan and Chmerkovskiy competed together on the show for nine weeks. Dewan, who has a dance background, proved to be a strong contender for the Mirrorball Trophy, often receiving high scores for routines that have ranged from jazz to quickstep.

However the pair’s run was interrupted when Chmerkovskiy was handed a one-week suspension, the show announced Oct. 17, due to a status he posted on TikTok that appeared to reference Will Smith’s notorious altercation with Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars. The pro had been reacting to the harsh critique that judge Carrie Ann Inaba gave his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson who’s paired up with actor Harry Shum Jr.
As a result, Chmerkovskiy missed the show’s signature Dedication Night. And Dewan was instead paired up with pro Alan Bersten for that week.
Chmerkovskiy has since apologized for the incident.

“I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention,” he wrote in his Instagram story, referencing Smith’s words to Rock amid the Oscars spat, “Keep my wife’s name out of your f------ mouth.”
Dewan told Women’s Health that she “did not foresee having as many challenges as I did that were thrown at me during my Dancing with the Stars journey.”

“However, the challenges of it gave me an opportunity to walk my talk, and I always think that when that happens, you can go back to your true north, to what’s your intention for doing something,” she told the outlet. “How do you want to show up as a human when you’re experiencing challenges? And I kept going back to my kids.”
She added that when the mid-season suspension went down, she chose to take the high road.
“I thought, ‘I have a real opportunity here. I can be annoyed and bitter and upset about this, or I can show up with grace and love and joy and focus on the moment,’” she told Women’s Health.
Dewan also said that she was intent on keeping her attention on her family. After all, that week’s Dedication Night dance was an ode to her mother.

“She was in town, thrilled to have this dance with me, and thrilled to experience this moment. And I thought that this is something she’s going to remember,” Dewan said. “We’re all going to remember my family forever. Let’s focus on that, and let’s not worry about all of this that’s going on.”
As the rest of the season shakes out, the actor shared a few more thoughts in an Instagram post Nov. 14. In it, she reflected on returning to dance, a craft that she’s long enjoyed.

“There’s something beautiful about returning to what you love, not as the person you once were, but as everything you’ve become,” Dewan wrote. “To everyone who showed up for us, voted, cheered and sent love… thank you!!! I felt it all ❤️”
She also had some lovely words for Chmerkovskiy.
“To Val- to learn from one of the best to ever do it is a gift I’ll treasure forever!” she wrote. “Thank you for your passion, creativity and friendship throughout this entire crazy ride🙏🏻”

title: Tyriq Withers, Daniel Kaluuya Go Viral For Hilariously Chaotic Local News Interview Amid FAA Ground Stop
summary: Tyriq Withers and Daniel Kaluuya, who were scheduled to be on a flight to Los Angeles, joined local television station KVAL in Eugene, Oregon, to share their take on the situation.
story: While the nationwide ground stop threw travelers across the country into chaos Nov. 13, actors Tyriq Withers and Daniel Kaluuya certainly made the most of their interrupted plans.
The two, who were scheduled to be on a flight to Los Angeles, joined local television station KVAL in Eugene, Oregon, to share their take on the situation.
While the interview started out quite ordinarily, with Withers speaking about how he and Kaluuya were forced to deboard amid the news, things quickly took a hilarious turn.
“It’s really upsetting me and my home girl because if you can’t go to the airport, where the hell can you go?” Withers told KVAL, before his “home girl” Kaluuya dissolved into giggles.

The “Him” actor, of course, referenced the viral Bella Noche nightclub meme from a 2015 news segment in which a partygoer, identified as Hazel London, reacted to a violence at the Baton Rouge nightclub with the now-famous phrase, “Well damn. If you can’t go to Bella Noche’s then where the hell can you go?!”

The Federal Aviation Administration halted departures for more than four hours due to what the agency said was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Later on, officials said that ground stop was due to an equipment outage that disrupted radar feeds and communications with aircraft.The FAA lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET.
During the interview with KVAL, Kaluuya kept things light, sharing that he was “grateful” that they were safe.

“I feel grateful. Obviously, it’s an inconvenience, but I feel grateful,” Kaluuya told the outlet. “I feel grateful because it could have happened any other way. Think about how many lives we probably saved because of that decision.”
He and Withers ended their segment by hyping up Eugene, Oregon.
Now that’s one way to pass the time!

title: Mom of ‘Breaking Bad’ Star RJ Mitte Shares Heartbreaking Tribute 1 Month After His Death
summary: Dyna Mitte, the mother of RJ Mitte, shared a moving tribute to the late “Breaking Bad” actor on the recent one-month anniversary of his death.
story: Dyna Mitte, the mother of RJ Mitte, shared a moving tribute to the late “Breaking Bad” actor on the recent one-month anniversary of his death.
In the post shared on Instagram Nov. 13,  Dyna Mitte reflected on the weeks since RJ Mitte died by suicide. He was 34.
Written as an open letter to the late actor, Dyna Mitte said that she misses him “so much it hurts.”

“My beautiful boy, it has been a month since you left us. I miss you so much it hurts,” Dyna Mitte wrote. “There are days that it feels like it happen today, and at times it feels like forever ago. I am trying to navigate through this new life, but it is so painfully difficult.”

RJ Mitte, best known for his role as Walter “Flynn” White Jr. on “Breaking Bad,” was also a philanthropist and disability rights advocate. He died on Oct. 12 in Brownsville, Texas, where lived, the Brownsville Justice of the Peace confirmed.

Dyna Mitte previously told NBC News that actor had no history of mental illness, however he had been going through a difficult emotional time. Still, he made no indication that he might end his life, she said.
In her latest post, Dyna Mitte wrote that she wished she could “just look” at her son again.
“What I would not give to hold you again, see that beautiful smile, laugh at the crazy conversations we had, are just look at you,” she wrote. “I love you forever + time.”
Dyna Mitte concluded her post with a wish.
“Please continue to watch over us,” she wrote. “With all my love, Mom”

The tribute comes after RJ Mitte’s sister Lacianne Carriere also opened up about her struggles with her grief. In an Oct. 24 Instagram post, Carriere wrote that she had been having a difficult time, wrapping her mind around his death.

“I just really need my brother right now…You would put on some lofi music and tell me to get up and go sit in the shower, how it always makes you feel better,” she wrote. “I know you’re telling me right now that I’ll be okay though I don’t know how I will. But I promise I’m going to do my hardest and I promise your love will always live through me until the day I see you again.”

title: Beyoncé Reveals New Details Around Her ‘Very Small’ Private 2008 Wedding to Jay-Z
summary: In a recent interview with British publication i-D Magazine, Queen Bey revealed that her nuptials were a complete surprise to the couple’s wedding guests.
story: Hold up — Beyoncé just gave us a few more deets about her 2008 wedding to media mogul Jay-Z.
In a recent interview with British publication i-D Magazine, Queen Bey revealed that her nuptials were a complete surprise to the couple’s wedding guests.

“We had a very small wedding in our home,” the musician said in the interview, published Nov. 11. “We told the guests we were having a party, and no one knew they were coming to our wedding but our parents and a few friends.”

Beyoncé and Jay-Z tied the knot on April 4, 2008, with the date (4/4) being a nod to the couple’s birthdays: Beyonce was born on September 4 while Jay-Z was born on December 4. Several stars, including Beyoncé’s former Destiny’s Child bandmates, Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams, and Gwyneth Paltrow, were spotted that day outside Jay-Z’s Tribeca home.
But little has been shared about the intimate wedding over the years.
In the interview with i-D, the singer said that her mother Tina Knowles, who had served as the stylist for Destiny’s Child’s for years, designed her wedding dress.
“My favourite dress my mother designed was my wedding dress—it was gorgeously simple and made with her love,” she told the outlet.
The “Cowboy Carter” singer told the outlet that the ensemble is one of her most cherished looks.
“Wearing a dress she designed was very important to me, and more important than any designer dress,” Beyoncé told i-D.
The artist, who’s been with Jay-Z for over two decades, shares three children with the rapper: Blue Ivy Carter, 14, and twins Rumi and Sir Carter, 9.

The couple has been famously private about their family life. Beyoncé shared a few seconds of footage from their wedding day in her 2011 live video for song “I Was Here.” Years later in 2015, Jay-Z shared a video from their big day on Instagram in a since-deleted post.

title: ‘Emo Gods’ Hoobastank, Simple Plan Surprised Fans on Plane With Mid-Air Performances
summary: While most travelers across the U.S. navigated chaos during the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop Nov.
story: While most travelers across the U.S. navigated chaos during the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop Nov. 13, some lucky flyers had a day that would make any millennial who sported emo bangs and fingerless gloves in high school proud.
Several alt rock acts, including Hoobastank and Simple Plan, showed up at a Southwest flight and performed some of their hits for those on board.

The flight, which left out of Los Angeles, had just missed the ground stop, so the bands were able to rock out for the passengers at 35,000 feet in the air, according to a press release about the event.
Fan videos posted to social media captured the performances. And when Hoobastank began playing their 2004 smash hit “The Reason” down the aisles, the crowd couldn’t help but sing.
A clip shared on the band’s official Instagram page shows the plane full of passengers, holding up their phones with the flashlight feature on, swaying to the acoustic set.
Another from the flight shows Simple Plan, performing their 2002 song “I’m Just A Kid.”
Other performers included The Used, who played their 2002 single “The Taste of Ink” and LØLØ.

According to a press release about the event, the bands showed up to a flight that was part of Southwest’s “Live at 35” music program, which features pop-up performances. This particular gig took place just ahead of the Vans Warped Tour Orlando stop this weekend at Camping World Stadium Campus.
The performances certainly brought a bit of levity to an otherwise frustrating day for travelers. People across social media couldn’t help but be just a bit jealous of those on board.
“this is the worst fomo I’ve ever had” one person wrote on social media.
Same, same.

title: Ron Howard Reveals the 1 Person He Wishes He Could Have Met — And Why
summary: Actor and filmmaker Ron Howard reveals the inspiration behind his documentary “Avedon,” how the film parallels his own life and the person he wishes he’d met.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Commercial Break,” TODAY.com catches up with guests between takes in Studio 1A for unfiltered moments and more questions.
If you’re wondering if Ron Howard is really the down-to-earth person everyone says he is, the answer is unequivocally yes.
Before we sit down to talk about Howard’s latest project, a documentary on acclaimed photographer Richard Avedon, we chat with Ice-T in the TODAY Lounge next to Studio 1A.
The pair strike up a conversation about Howard’s recent projects, including “Avedon” and the upcoming film “Alone At Dawn,” starring Anne Hathaway and Adam Driver.
Howard is called to set for his segment. As he leaves, Ice-T points after him and tells me, “He’s the OG.”

After getting his start on the “Andy Griffith Show” at the age of 6, Howard, 72, has maintained a steady show biz career, first in acting, then directing, for more 65 years. In the process, he’s earned two Oscars and dozens of nominations for films including “A Beautiful Mind,” “Frost/Nixon,” “Apollo 13,” “Parenthood,” “Cocoon” and “Hillbilly Elegy,” not to mention five Emmys for his work in television.

Howard has also earned a reputation for being one of the nicest guys in Hollywood. It’s one he fully lives up to when he catches up with TODAY.com backstage to talk about “Avedon,” the advice he gives his daughter, Bryce Dallas Howard, and the one person he’d have lunch with if he could.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

Slowly, because he didn’t give a lot of interviews. Now we found two or three that were great and he’s very open. He’s very articulate, very funny, but he was guarded. For that reason, we had to dig through those archives to find him on camera, to find him telling his story.

We did find some old audio tapes that were damaged, but digitally now we’re able to repair those and make those something that we could really use in the film. So, there’s more of him in this documentary than you’ve ever seen before.
So, the man behind the camera slowly but surely, in my mind, became the central figure in this documentary and became really the story of a really great artist and a fascinating guy.

You’re really not alone. Again, he was very careful. So in certain circles, he’s known, he’s studied. I didn’t know much beyond the name, you know? He was a kind of a brand, but I had no idea the range of his work.
I also didn’t recognize how much he did do as a kind of a social documentarian. The civil rights movement, Andy Warhol, political unrest, Vietnam.

He was also, like a lot of good journalists, really interested in exposing hypocrisy through his lens. And he was pretty good at catching people off guard and revealing little insights that maybe weren’t so flattering.
We’re very different personalities, but I do see some parallels. And it is a love of the work and an excitement with what you can share, but also just what you get from it. I mean, he fed off of it.
I like to think that I have a little better work life balance than he was able to achieve. In the doc, he admits that that’s a regret of his.

But his ability to straddle the commercial world, magazines, TV commercials, glamour and celebrity and all of that, and also really offer us this very insightful understanding of some of the edgier sides and aspects of society where people are suffering and there’s real struggle.
And he brought the same energy, focus, creative ambition and integrity to all of it.

I’m really interested in high achievers, the world they inhabit, but also their process and their impact on their personal lives,  because that’s always interesting to me is how do they, what kind of balance did they find?

In Avedon’s case, he was admittedly a workaholic, the family side of his life was something that he had some regrets about later on, and we didn’t shy away from that. Nor did his family members who were willing to be very, very open. Loving, but honest.
So I think that’s really what I want to try to discover and share: What makes these people outliers and what makes them utterly relatable to all of us as well?
My father was from the Midwest, a farm boy. But he had this kind of, I call it “Midwestern zen.” It was this sort of practical understanding of the duality of life.

You know, he changed the course of the family history. He and my mom, both from the Midwest, my mom from a small town, my dad from a farm, taking this huge chance to try to get into show business. They didn’t know anybody. They didn’t have a prayer, and yet they worked their way into this world and they made a life.

That’s inspiring to me. Neither reached the heights that they dreamed of when they were 18 or 19 years old and taking that leap, but they made a living and they made lives in this business, without bitterness and anger, but with this ongoing appreciation for just what it was to be a part of the storytelling process.
And this kind of balanced view of the world that I think gave them peace of mind. I’ve always appreciated it.
Oh. Man, man, man. Wow, one person. Let me really think about it because it’s a really interesting question ...
It sounds crazy, but I would really like to be able to sit down and talk to Buster Keaton.
He started off as a child actor, a performer in Vaudeville, rose to these heights, struggled, went through the silent era, into the talking era, then had a resurgence in television.

He actually, I think, probably had a greater understanding of the origins of American cinema and the sort of Hollywood entertainment system of anyone, and in this very earthy, practical kind of way. And so, given my life, you know, he was decades before me.
I think I would really, really enjoy getting his sense of what the earliest days were like and what it felt like to transition all the way into live television and beyond.

title: Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy Break Down  ‘The Good Daughter’ Ending, From Emotional Moments to Plot Twists
summary: Warning: Spoilers ahead for “The Good Daughter.” The new Peacock series takes a turn when it comes to discovering who was behind the sisters’ trauma, shooting and more.
story: Warning: Spoilers ahead for “The Good Daughter.”
Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy bring to life author Karin Slaughter’s best-selling psychological thriller “The Good Daughter” in the new Peacock series, out Nov. 12.

The actors portray trauma-bonded yet resilient, estranged sisters Charlotte “Charlie” (Fahy) and Samantha “Sam” (Byrne) Quinn, who reunite after one of them unintentially becomes involved in a murder case involving a young student.

Over the course of the six-episode miniseries, viewers discover how an attack on their family when the sisters were teens ended with the death of mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), life-altering injuries for Sam, Charlie being sexually assaulted and their defense attorney father Rusty (Brendon Gleeson) forever changed.

Flash forward over two decades later, and the sisters, both lawyers, are reunited after Sam returns to town to help her father with a case. After a one-night stand with a man named Mason “Huck” (Jake McDorman), Charlie visits him at the school he works at and witnesses a shooting.

An 18-year-old named Kelly (Shayna Benardo) is accused of shooting Principal Douglas Pinkman and another student. But something doesn’t add up. As the family gets involved in the case, the sisters become haunted by their past attackers and townspeople, who blame them for what they believe are injustices.
The final episode, titled “What Really Happened,” does just that, revealing who actually shot Pinkman. It also shares more insight into who was involved in the sisters’ attack.

“It’s very rare for anyone to figure out the real truth of this story, and that’s by design. And I’ve been plotting thrillers for a long time,” author and showrunner Slaughter tells TODAY.com. “I think it was one of my strengths to make you think one thing, and then suddenly it’s another. I love playing with expectations that way. Anybody who wants a good thriller will be wholly satisfied.”

“But you know,” she adds, “one of the things about writing a thriller about families is there’s also emotional suspense, and that underlying tension of what’s going on between Sam and Charlie, and where we’re going to leave them propels you through the show as much as the whodunit.”
Here’s what happens at the end of “The Good Daughter.”

Mason was one of the men who was present when their mom was shot and they were attacked. Ben (Michael Dorman), Charlie’s estranged husband and Pikeville’s assistant district attorney, finds Mason’s written confession inside Rusty’s home.
The sisters previously knew that Zach Culpepper Jr. was behind the attack, but because the other man called his accomplice “brother,” they assumed it was his sibling Daniel Culpepper. It wasn’t.

Mason had given Zach Culpepper Jr. $5,000 to kill Rusty after he successfully represented a man in court who sexually assaulted Mason’s sister. Rusty got the man a lighter sentence, and Mason’s sister killed herself, so he wanted revenge.

During the attack, Mason was able to talk Zach out of killing the sisters and pushed him off Charlie when she was being sexually assaulted, but the damage was done. He told the sisters he tried to confess, but his parents wouldn’t let him.

After Rusty dies, his daughters are tasked with executing his final wishes. While going through his office, they discover dozens of letters that read “You Owe Me,” and $2,000 checks made out to Zach Culpepper Jr.

After Mason’s confession, they realize that Zach Jr. was being paid every month to keep the truth quiet about Mason’s involvement in the Quinn family attack. Mason insisted it was his parents who made the deal and he found out 10 years ago.

Mason first confessed to Rusty after he found out about the hush payments when his mother was dying. Rusty did not want his daughters to relive their trauma and become entrenched in a new trail, so he had Mason hand over the money that was for Zach Jr and write down his confession, which Ben later found.
Asked if Rusty forgave him, Mason said no.
Why did Rusty want to control the money? Mason said it was so that one day Charlie and Sam could decide if they wanted to keep paying Zach Jr. or show Mason’s confession to the cops.
They call the cops on Mason, but for a different reason. Mason had stolen the gun Kelly used to shoot Principal Pinkman. If he got convicted for taking the weapon, he would get 10 years in prison.

The sisters and Ben discuss their options, breaking down how even if Zach Jr. stops getting paid and Zach Sr. confesses Mason’s involvement, a long legal battle would ensue. Their discussion brings them back to Kelly’s case and if she was responsible for Principal Pinkman’s death.
Kelly brought a gun to school and did plan to shoot Principal Doug, but as Charlie and Sam discover, it wasn’t her idea.
During Kelly’s court cases, it is revealed that she is pregnant. But who is the father? It’s actually Principal Pinkman.
The principal’s wife, Judith (Paula Malcomson), was the one who orchestrated the shooting. Charlie goes over to Judith’s home and Judith confesses.

Judith witnessed her husband sexually assaulting Kelly and learned that the teen was pregnant. Her husband told her that they would take care of the baby, which infuriated her. Judith then kept scaring Kelly about her and her baby’s future, until she convinced her to kill her husband.

The day of the shooting, Judith put her fingers over Kelly’s hand and pulled the trigger. She struggled to take the gun from Kelly, and they accidentally shot another other student. Judith said she planned on also shooting Kelly to avoid the teen confessing, but she didn’t have enough bullets. Her plan to be seen as the mourning widow and get her husband’s insurance money was unsuccessful.
As Judith confesses, Charlie records their conversation, while Sam and Ben listen from outside. Judith loads her gun and demands that Charlie leave her home. Judith then kills herself.
With Judith’s confession, Kelly gets five years of prison time since she was still involved in the murders.
The series ends with Charlie and Sam back at Rusty’s, going through his belongings. Ben and Charlie have decided they are moving to Atlanta.

Meanwhile, the sisters are looking for a photo of their mom that their dad had wanted them to find. They find the photo in the back of another picture frame. On the back it has a message for them, “Last word.”
Byrne tells TODAY.com she wouldn’t want to tell the audience what to feel or think, but at the end, part of her hopes the sisters continue to work on their relationship.
“The reconciliation is such a joyful thing,” she says, adding that she hopes they continue to be “in one another’s lives.”
Fahy agrees, also telling TODAY.com, “I really imagine that when we leave them, they are in each other’s lives in a big and beautiful way moving forward.”

title: Avril Lavigne Announces Birth of First Child, a Baby Girl — See the Pics
summary: Avril Lavigne just announced the cutest damn thing.
story: Avril Lavigne just announced the cutest damn thing.
The punk rocker shared on Instagram Nov. 13 that she just welcomed her first child. And the “Sk8er Boi” singer made the announcement in a way that would make any millennial emo kid proud.
“Our Mini F------ Princess has arrived 🎀👑🍼🩷,” Lavigne wrote in the post.
The 42-year-old mom did not reveal the identity of the child’s father.

In the Instagram post, Lavigne shared a series of photos, including one that featured what appeared to be the rocker’s hand and that of her mystery partner, holding their newborn’s tiny fingers. Another snap showed Lavigne, clutching her baby girl who’s decked out in a leopard print onesie.
The final photo in the slideshow features three pairs of Vans sneakers on a skateboard, symbolizing the new family of three. The snap also appears to be a sweet nod to her 2002 hit “Sk8er Boi.”

Lavigne, who’s best known for her 2002 debut album “Let Go,” has been relatively private about her personal life. However, she’s had several high-profile relationships including a marriage to Sum 41’s Deryck Whibley from 2006 to 2010 and another to Nickelback’s Chad Kroeger from 2013 to 2015.
She was also briefly engaged to musician Mod Sun in 2022.

title: NFL Quarterback Sam Hartman Is Named the Next ‘Bachelor.’ The 1 Quality He Wants in a Match
summary: Bachelor Nation can add a new football player to its roster.
story: Bachelor Nation can add a new football player to its roster.
Sam Hartman, a quarterback for The Washington Commanders, was just revealed as the new star of “The Bachelor.”

The professional athlete joins a growing list of NFL players who have taken their quest for love to the ABC dating series over the years. Prior football players who have been the show’s lead include Jessie Palmer, who now hosts “The Bachelor,” and Colton Underwood.
The official Instagram page for “The Bachelor” shared a photo of Hartman Nov. 13, captioning the post, “the next Bachelor 🌹.”
Hartman also appeared on “Good Morning America” to discuss his upcoming season of the show, which will premiere on March 21 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC.

The 27-year-old admitted that he first said, “No way!” when asked to appear on “The Bachelor” since he was worried about “the connotation” of finding love on reality TV. But Palmer, a former football pro turned “Bachelor,” helped change his mind.
“He kind of gave me the inside and gave me kind of what it is, what it’s not,” he said.
The Charlotte, N.C. native said he’s seeking one key characteristic in his future partner: competitiveness.

“(I’m looking for) competitiveness in somebody that I want to be able to chase. Not chase in a way that you haven’t texted me back in a week, but chase in a way that they have a drive for something and motivate me every day to wake up and chase them,” he said.

Hartman, who played college football for Wake Forest University and the University of Notre Dame, said he’s also looking for a woman with “compassion,” possibly someone who works in a field where they provide “some type of caregiving.”
“My whole family is in the medicine field,” he said.
Hartman spoke about his upcoming adventure on “The Bachelor”  the morning after his team beat the New York Giants in a Nov. 12 match.
The NFL player is used to being calm under pressure while playing in packed stadiums, but he admitted that he’s “very nervous” to start his journey on “The Bachelor.”
“I have a tough time holding a conversation with one girl. Thirty is gonna be pretty tough,” he said.
Hartman’s teammates have been giving him some words of wisdom as he prepares to find love. But he joked that he’s “probably not gonna listen” to their advice.
The quarterback doesn’t expect to find somebody who’s as skilled at football as he is, but said the ladies vying for his attention will certainly have to show off their football skills.
“They’ve gotta be ready to bring their competitive spirit,” he said.

title: How ‘I Play Rocky’ Actor Anthony Ippolito Nailed the Iconic Sylvester Stallone Voice
summary: At first listen, Anthony Ippolito’s voice in biographical Sylvester Stallone film “I Play Rocky” is startling, not because of its tenor or pitch — but because of its striking familiarity.
story: At first listen, Anthony Ippolito’s voice in biographical Sylvester Stallone film “I Play Rocky” is startling, not because of its tenor or pitch — but because of its striking familiarity.

That husky, unmistakable New York accent is what so many “Rocky” fans have grown up hearing against the film’s rough, Philadelphia backdrop and that symphonic Bill Conti soundtrack. And yet, the speaker isn’t Stallone at all.

Ippolito, who plays Sly in the film, spoke to TODAY.com ahead of the film’s nationwide release Nov. 20. He said that he was well aware that the character was profoundly meaningful to people across different generations, so he “didn’t take it lightly.”
And that meant doing some intense research, unearthing as much footage as he could from Stallone’s early years when Sly was still trying to make it in acting.
“It was actually pretty difficult in some ways because he wasn’t a huge movie star at that point,” Ippolito said.
He added that he “just really wanted to find everything I could on him and put my best foot forward.”

Based on Stallone’s own life, the film tells the story of a young Sly, who’s desperate to get his film career going, but sees little promise in actually nabbing a substantial role. With few prospects and a baby on the way, the doggedly ambitious Stallone decides that the only sure-fire path to success is by writing a blockbuster film — and casting himself as the lead. The story, one that peels back the curtain on how the now-timeless “Rocky” was truly made, ultimately explores the power of belief in oneself and the indomitable human spirit.

But bringing to the screen an authentic portrayal of Stallone — a man whose reputation as a heroic action star has risen to near-legendary levels — was no simple task. And Ippolito says he was up for the challenge.

“It was a lot to take in and a little daunting at the beginning, especially. But I was also excited. I think that this part of his story is one that some people knew, but not enough,” Ippolito tells TODAY.com. “So I was really happy to have any hand in helping you know people understand this part of it because it’s incredible.

Ippolito, who did not have a voice coach for the gig, explains that he perfected the voice by watching any clips he could find of old Stallone interviews and the action star’s early supporting roles. He also said that much of his prepwork involved understanding Stallone’s partial facial paralysis and how it impacted his speech. Stallone was delivered by a physician who used forceps to pull him out, Sly has said on many occasions. The delivery left him with a severed facial nerve on his left side.

“That facial paralysis caused by the birth accident with forceps created this change in his voice and also a bit of a slur,” Ippolito said. “He had to grow up dealing with that and dealing with the judgment that came with that over the course of his youth.”

Luckily, Ippolito was also able to get some tips from Sly himself. It’s something, Ippolito says, that was particularly useful as details about the nascent stages of his career aren’t so widely available or publicized.

“This really isn’t about that period of time after Rocky where he became a star. It was more so about the period of struggle and loneliness and isolation that he was in,” Ippolito explains. “Getting to speak to him about that period of time was really really helpful, getting to hear firsthand the toll that that takes on you growing up and the types of adversity that he was facing.”
Ippolito says that he felt “privileged” to learn from the man himself.

“It’s kind of a vulnerable thing, right? This is a very pivotal time in his life, and it’s a not very polished period of time,” he says. “I just really appreciated him 50 years after the fact being able to share it with me.”

Stallone, of course, has seen the film and he’s been open about how impressed he’s been with Ippolito’s portrayal. Even in the project’s earliest stages, Stallone was already moved by Ippolito’s commitment to the character.
“The text that Sly sent us after we watched Anthony’s tape, I’ll never forget,” producer Toby Emmerich told NBC News. “He said, ‘This is not an impersonation. This is a performance.’”
Ippolito’s reaction is one of humility.
“He was very, very kind,” Ippolito says.

title: See a First Look at Mel and Jack With Their Baby as ‘Virgin River’ Is Officially Renewed for Season 9
summary: “Virgin River” has officially been renewed for a landmark Season 9 on Netflix. See a photo of what’s ahead for Mel and Jack as they welcome a baby to their family.
story: “Virgin River” has officially been renewed for a landmark Season 9 on Netflix, becoming the longest-running original scripted drama series on the platform, and TODAY.com has an exclusive first look at what’s ahead.

The Season 9 renewal comes ahead of the release of Season 8, which is set to premiere in 2027. Last season ended on a major cliffhanger as Mel and Jack finally became parents but had to rush their newborn son into emergency surgery.

TODAY.com can exclusively share a new photo from Episode 1 of Season 8 of the characters, played by Alexandra Breckenridge and Martin Henderson, sharing a sweet moment with their baby boy. In the photo, an emotional Jack holds his son as Mel stares lovingly into her husband’s eyes and rests a hand on the baby’s head.
It’s a well-deserved moment of peace for the couple, whose challenging journey to parenthood has been a major focal point of the show.

In Season 7, they agreed to adopt the unborn child of a young woman named Marley (Rachel Drance) then found their future hanging in the balance as Marley’s ex-boyfriend (and the father of her child) came to town. Marley decided to go through with the adoption, then learned her baby had a congenital heart defect and would need emergency surgery after birth.
An exact premiere date for Season 8 hasn’t been announced yet, but the season will premiere next year.

In addition to releasing a sneak peek at Season 8, Netflix gave fans a double dose of glee Nov. 13 as the streaming service announced Season 9’s renewal, which will have 10 episodes. “Virgin River” is based on Robyn Carr’s book series of the same name, which has more than 20 installments.

“I’m incredibly proud of our show and couldn’t be more thrilled to have the opportunity to continue into Season 9!” Breckenridge said in a statement. “Everyone on our production works so hard to make the world of ‘Virgin River’ come alive. It’s truly been a gift to be here,” she said.
Henderson echoed his co-star’s sentiments.
“It’s staggering to think we are still making ‘Virgin River’ after all these years and I’m delighted to get to play the role of Jack for the ninth straight season!” he said in a statement.

The actor thanked the show’s fans, saying the cast and crew “wouldn’t be here without them all,” and he said they’re eager to “keep making it to the best of our ability” as long as fans want to watch the show.

title: The Gift Robert Irwin Gave Witney Carson’s Sons That They’re Already Sharing With Baby No. 3
summary: Witney Carson says everyone in her family is preparing for the arrival of her third baby in their own exciting way, especially her sons Kevin Leo and Jet Carson.
story: Witney Carson says everyone in her family is preparing for the arrival of her third baby in their own exciting way, especially her sons Kevin Leo and Jet Carson.
The “Dancing With the Stars” pro announced in August that she was pregnant and by September revealed she was having another boy.

“Every day, I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, I’m actually going to have three babies.’ So some days I’m overwhelmed, and some days I’m feeling very excited,” she tells TODAY.com. “And I think the boys are very excited too.”
Her sons are so thrilled to have a baby brother that they’re already sharing their toys with baby on the way, including a gift from Robert Irwin.

“Robert Irwin gifted them two huge crocodiles, and they put them in baby brother’s crib because they really want baby brother to sleep with these two huge crocodiles,” Carson says. “So they’re doing little things like that that are very sweet and thoughtful.”
Carson and Irwin competed on and won Season 34 of “DWTS”together, cultivating a great friendship with each other’s families in the process.
She loves that her sons are “thinking about” their sibling, “which is so cute.” However, she notes, “The crocodile, he won’t be sleeping with those. But it was a good thought.”

Just like her sons have already done a sweet gesture for their brother, Carson is also giving back and partnering with Pampers to give 50 families the chance to win $1,500 to help fulfill their registries.
The dancer says she hopes to relieve any stress when it comes to expenses, which “can really add up.”
“At a time where it’s supposed to be very exciting, we want to take that load off parents and allow them to just enjoy.”

She also understands how wonderful it is to have the support of friends and family during a pregnancy. But one thing she was so happy about was feeling the love from other parents while competing on Season 35 with Guillermo Rodriguez.

“I love being a mom and I love to dance. And so the fact that I could do both was such a huge blessing. And I really did prove to myself that I could do it, and I think in turn it kind of showed other women that as well,” Carson, who is due in February, says. “Which wasn’t my  mission or anything, but it really just kind of turned into that.”
She adds that the support she felt from parents, from moms, “from people who really were cheering me on and rooting for me felt so empowering.”
“And that really allowed me to keep going day by day, to keep doing better, to keep showing up,” she says.

title: Highlights from Pope Leo’s historic, 12-day tour of South America
summary: They turned out in their millions to greet Pope Leo as he made his way around Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on a gruelling 12-day tour of the South America.
story: LIMA, Peru — They turned out in their millions to greet Pope Leo as he made his way around Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on a grueling 12-day tour of the South American nations, weeks after undergoing successful surgery for lung cancer.
Pope keeps energetic pace in trip to South America after surgery

For some — particularly those in Argentina, which had not received a papal visit since Pope John Paul II in 1987 — it was the first time they would get to see a pontiff in person. A record 2.5 million people flooded onto the streets of Buenos Aires last week to try and catch a glimpse of Leo.

The Vatican dubbed it a “homecoming” tour for the 71-year-old, as the Chicago-born pontiff, who is also a citizen of Peru, spent the final six days in the country where he lived for decades and served as a bishop until 2023.
NBC News takes a look at some of the highlights from his trip.
Montevideo, Uruguay

After a 17-hour flight from Rome, Leo and his entourage touched down in Uruguay’s capital, Montevideo. Praising the Lord and thanking his wonderful medical assistants, Leo said that while some had questioned whether he would be able to make the trip because of his recent surgery, he “had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward.”

title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented  meeting on the sidelines of APEC, officials say
summary: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.
story: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.

“President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People’s Republic of China and the president of the Russian Federation,” Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said in a call with reporters Friday night. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”

It is not anticipated that any sort of agreement will come from the trilateral meeting, according to a senior U.S. official, who described the session as an “entry point” and “the first conversation,” pointing to the reduction of nuclear arsenals as a key topic.

“We do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the senior U.S. official said about the issue of nuclear weapons.

Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
The three-way summit with Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin comes at a complicated moment in relations for the three countries.

Trump intends to discuss the Iran war with the two leaders, but not the war in Ukraine, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that discussions about the war in Ukraine are a separate “track” that China is not part of so it would not be “appropriate.”

Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.
There is no bilateral with Putin scheduled, but the two leaders will appear at events and the trilateral meeting together, according to a senior U.S. official.
There are no plans for Trump to engage with North Korea during the trip, according to a senior U.S. official.

Separately, Elon Musk will be the only business leader who is part of the president’s delegation, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that other U.S. business leaders will attend the summit in their own capacity but there is no official U.S. business delegation.
Musk will not be part of any official meetings, according to a senior U.S. official.

Two senior U.S. officials said that they don’t think Trump will raise the espionage investigation focused on Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence agent who allegedly had a romantic relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, with China.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip. In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” a senior U.S. official said. “These are national security matters that we develop in the administration and interagency process, and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there.”
Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit
By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China’s growing clout and prestige.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
For Subscribers

“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signaling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they’re making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don’t like,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
For Subscribers

The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.

More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China’s argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia’s war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.

The trilateral meeting could undercut China’s push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism,” he said.
The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years
Putin and Xi are no strangers. They’ve fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.”

Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the No. 1 trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.

As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia’s energy resources and became Moscow’s principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.

In the lead-up to Russia’s war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship.” China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv’s Western allies played a part in provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine.
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing’s policy on issues related to Taiwan.

Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.

Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which the leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalized plans for establishing the United Nations.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can’t be enforced on others.

“It’s clear that a meeting between the leaders of countries such as Russia, China and the United States is extremely significant,” Peskov said. “However, let’s not forget that the vision for a global order is that no one tries to impose any particular view of global order, and it should be based entirely on mutual benefit and mutual respect.”

title: Pope Leo makes emotional return to his ‘beloved diocese of Chiclayo’
summary: Pope Leo XIV made a triumphant return to the Peruvian city of Chiclayo, where he served as bishop for and was affectionately nicknamed “Padre Roberto.”
story: LIMA, Peru — Pope Leo XIV made a triumphant return Friday to the Peruvian city of Chiclayo, where he served as bishop for eight years and was affectionately nicknamed “Padre Roberto.”

Leo arrived in a plane decorated with “#LeoXFliesHome” stickers and he was greeted with a sign at the airport bearing the same message. A small dance troupe performed before him as he stepped onto the tarmac.
He will stay in the area until Sunday to lead eight events, including a private dinner with the priests who once reported to him as bishop.
The crowds greeting Leo in Peru’s fourth-largest city were smaller than the estimated 3 million or so who welcomed the pope when he arrived Wednesday in Lima, the country’s capital.
The Vatican estimated that 1 million people had lined the motorcade route to the Mass and that 500,000 attended.

title: Microsoft services hit by major outage across the world
summary: A widespread outage continued to hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Friday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts.
story: A massive global outage impacting more than a dozen Microsoft cloud services, including Outlook email and Teams messaging stretched into Friday as the tech giant struggled to restore the service, which is critical to the day-to-day functions of governments, schools and businesses around the world.

Starting around 12:50 p.m. ET Thursday, Microsoft began warning users of its products on social media that it was “investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online,” its cloud email service.
By the time workers were arriving at the office on Friday morning, Microsoft said it was still working on the problem.

Microsoft said in its latest update about 7 a.m. ET that it was seeing “encouraging recovery progress in Europe, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. “
It added that “North America is also improving; however, some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue.”
Hours earlier the tech giant had warned that attempts “to improve serviceability” were “not taking as expected,” it said in an update on X overnight.
Some on the social media platform derided the technical responses, or hoped email would be down Friday for a possible day off.
There are few products as pervasive inside global companies as Outlook email.
Email traffic to many of the tech giant’s 450 million users came to a halt around midday, with email programs freezing and crashing, and mobile devices unable to refresh inboxes or send messages.

The problems also affected Microsoft’s non-commercial consumer products, according to a notice on its website. “This issue impacts Outlook.com, OneDrive, OneNote To Do, Teams, and Microsoft 365 for the web.”

Throughout the day the problems spread. As of 11 p.m. ET on Thursday, Microsoft’s online status pages said its corporate services Exchange Online, Copilot, Microsoft Planner, Sharepoint, Microsoft To Do, Windows 365, cloud printing services, and mobile device management programs were all experiencing issues.

The problem caused chaos in workplaces around the world. At one, truck manufacturer Workhouse Group, it forced the company to delay its earnings report which was set to be released on Thursday afternoon.
In a statement, Workhorse said: “The rescheduling is due to business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outages taking place today.”

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office, the L.A. County Sheriff’s Department and other government agencies in California said their communications were impacted by the outage, NBC Los Angeles reported. In Washington, email services at federal agencies and on Capitol Hill were impacted.

In Colorado, the Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office said the outage was affecting online bond payments for people being held in its detention facility. “Until Outlook email is restored, anyone needing to post bond for immediate release must do so in person at the jail,” it said on social media.

Throughout most of the day, Microsoft has said it has been working on the issue. By 2:50 p.m. ET, the company wrote on social media that it was “testing a configuration change” to its cloud servers in order to try to restore services.
By 4:40 p.m. ET, the company said it was restarting “affected servers to return them to service.”
Microsoft explained a few minutes later in another post on X that a “core process on affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The company also said it was “shifting traffic” around in order to relieve overwhelmed servers that remained online.

But then not long after, the company again said, “The servers we returned to service can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic; we’re analyzing diagnostic data to determine what’s triggering the behavior.”

The updates continued into the night. At 11:36 p.m., Microsoft said it its efforts to improve server stability were ongoing, but that while it was “observing partial recovery across regions in which we’ve applied these adjustments” that didn’t result in “sustained recovery.”

NBC News attempted to reach Microsoft representatives through multiple phone numbers listed on the company’s press releases and through a phone number to its investor relations department, however the company has not commented in response.

An email sent to a public relations firm that represents Microsoft from a personal non-Outlook or Microsoft based email address quickly bounced back, with an error message reading that the server was “unavailable or unable to receive mail.”
In a statement to Bloomberg News, a Microsoft spokesperson said: “We appreciate our customers’ patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible.”

Major outages, such as Microsoft’s, are not unprecedented but have become increasingly rare. In 2024, a glitch with a security program led to Windows devices around the world freezing, causing them displaying Microsoft’s well-known “blue screen of death” error. That issue brought airlines, companies, and critical systems to a halt.
Some of Microsoft’s other critical cloud services, such as its Azure cloud computing platform, that powers many websites and apps, remained online and did not have any additional issues.

title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills at least six people, officials say
summary: An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.
story: An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.

The strike hit a surgery building at Nasser Hospital, with medical staff and patients among those killed, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, health officials said. The Israeli military said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants.

The strike — the latest despite an ongoing U.S.-backed ceasefire — shattered ceilings and left debris strewn across wards inside the hospital, which is one of the few functioning medical facilities left in Gaza after the destruction of Israel’s yearslong military assault.

Palestinian surgeon Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira was among those killed, the Health Ministry said. He was featured in the 2026 documentary “American Doctor,” which followed three American doctors helping to provide medical care in Gaza.

title: Ukraine faces new Starshield disruptions as Trump envoys meet with Putin
summary: Hours after an American delegation touched down in Moscow for peace talks, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s military had experienced a renewed wave of “significant disruptions” to the Starshield satellite internet service, hampering its ability to defend itself against Russia.
story: Hours after an American delegation touched down in Moscow for peace talks, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s military had experienced a renewed wave of “significant disruptions” to the Starshield satellite internet service, hampering its ability to defend itself against Russia.
“These are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions,” he said in a Telegram post. “For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones.”

His comments came as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, arrived in the Russian capital for peace talks with President Vladimir Putin, a day after trilateral talks aimed at ending the war were held in the United Arab Emirates.
The two-day Abu Dhabi summit, the first such meeting since February, ended with no major breakthrough, although representatives of Russia and Ukraine agreed on a large exchange of prisoners of war.
In Moscow, Kushner told ‌Putin that Europe wanted ‌a role ‌in future negotiations, according to Russia’s Tass state news agency.

European countries cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly after Putin launched his invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, but have since expressed concern about the Trump administration’s softening stance toward the Kremlin. Kushner last week said he also wanted to address “long-term European security and stability,” signaling a focus beyond just Ukraine that prompted a firm response from European leaders.

Expanding on that theme on Thursday, Kushner said there was a “very strong momentum and desire” from European leaders to “engage together,” adding that “understanding the long-term security between Russia, Ukraine, and Europe is a conversation that we started having with them.”

While representatives from several European countries were in Abu Dhabi, they did not play a direct role in the talks. Russian negotiators have previously opposed their involvement, citing Europe’s support for Kyiv as an obstacle.

At the meeting in Moscow, the Interfax news agency reported that Putin proposed a joint Russian-Ukrainian humanitarian mission to the city of Kostiantynivka ⁠in eastern ​Ukraine, similar to the Melania Trump-brokered mission in Oleshky that allowed residents to leave the Russian-controlled town.
Thursday’s talks were “substantive, constructive, frank and useful,” Putin’s aide Yuri Ushakov said.
Kushner and Witkoff met with Putin for about two hours before going to Dublin, where they met with Zelenskyy for more than an hour as the conflict stretches toward the five-year mark.

Zelenskyy in Dublin indicated the Europeans would not be on the sidelines. “Next meeting, Europe will be during negotiations, will be a negotiation team — not some way, not separately. They will have a voice,” he said.
The U.S. and Zelenskyy want Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.
Zelenskyy also said Thursday that military units had for several days reported internet speed restrictions affecting the entire front line and Russian-occupied parts of the country.

A limit of 100 mph is once again being “imposed on Starshield,” he said of the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink communications service. The system normally runs at a stable speed exceeding around 250 mph.
“These are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions,” he said. “For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones.”
“Unfortunately, there have already been strikes that got through because our interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds and are unable to intercept in time,” he added.
Zelenskyy added that Ukraine was trying to ⁠clarify the reasons for the ‌restriction with the ​U.S. side.
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment from NBC News.

Craig Albert, the graduate director of national defense studies at Augusta University, said decreasing Starshield’s speed would slow down how fast Ukraine’s offensive drones travel, “which makes them pretty much target practice for faster interceptor drones by the Russians.”
It would also slow down Ukrainian interceptor drones and their missile defense systems, meaning “Russian drones can get through their defenses much quicker.”

“The Russians can target more infrastructure, and the Ukrainians just don’t have the speed to counteract,” he said, adding that “for the price, the scale, the speed, the scalability, and the efficiency,” there were no real options other than Starshield.
Ukraine first raised the alarm last month about speed limits being imposed on Starshield, which is crucial to its battlefield operations and air defenses.

Starlink owner Elon Musk initially put the responsibility for the restrictions on Trump, who has been trying to pressure Kyiv to make concessions to end the war. The U.S. government said ​that any such decision could only have been ‌made by Musk.

Trump denied being involved in the decision concerning the slowdown. Musk later said in an X post that SpaceX had acted to close a “loophole” with its civilian Starlink service, accusing Ukraine of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using it for offensive drone strikes, which the country denied.
Moscow has so far resisted such efforts to bring Europe to the main negotiating table, something Ukraine has long sought.
The talks came against the backdrop of continued fighting on the front lines, where neither side has achieved significant progress for months.

Instead, the focus has shifted to daily attacks with long-range missiles and drones. Russia has targeted Ukrainian cities, aiming to cut off water and power supplies as winter sets in. Kyiv has resumed attacks on energy infrastructure, a campaign that drew Trump’s ire.
Ukrainian officials said Thursday that five civilians had been killed by Russian strikes on the country overnight, and 29 people injured. The Russian Defense Ministry said it had shot down 71 drones.

title: Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation
summary: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.
story: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.

Megaspeed’s statement came hours before the resignation of Huang, one of the leaders of the AI boom, who co-founded the American chipmaker and helped build it into the world’s second most valuable company.

In its first statement since reports emerged about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the future of the tech giant, Megaspeed said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.”
U.S. intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang had an affair with the Nvidia CEO and was a Chinese intelligence operative, a person with knowledge of the matter told NBC News on Sunday.

She held a senior position at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed is under U.S. criminal investigation for allegedly smuggling American-made chips into China in defiance of U.S. export controls.

A criminal investigation is ongoing in Singapore, where officials said Thursday Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the country. The government also issued her with a stern warning after finding that she had knowingly provided police with inaccurate information to downplay her role in the company. It said that Huang was not investigated for espionage.

The country’s Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement that authorities had interviewed Huang and impounded her passport in 2025, but that its requests for cooperation from U.S. authorities had gone unanswered.
“Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” it said.

Investigators concluded in February that there was “insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences,” the statement said, adding that investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals were continuing, related to the shipment of servers via Singapore.

Megaspeed, meanwhile, said in the statement Thursday that it has “cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.” The statement was signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.
It said that “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.”
